links.label: Ownership of the underlying

fields.value: spv-claim-redeemable

The token is, in the issuer's own words, 'a non-negotiable digital record evidencing a pro rata beneficial entitlement (if any)' as beneficiary of a BVI bare trust over a pooled holding of the referenced shares — with no entitlement to any specific identifiable share. Crucially, the trustee recognises only Trek Forge Ltd (a Backpack affiliate) as Tokenholder and sole beneficiary; a person holding the token in their own wallet 'becomes the on-chain holder of those Tokens for blockchain transfer purposes only' and has no redemption, distribution, instruction or enforcement right against the trust unless and until a 'Direct Redemption Contingency' occurs (Backpack insolvency, cessation, >90 days of suspended redemptions, court order, etc.) and the trustee expressly registers them. In practice a holder realises value by depositing the token back into a KYC'd Backpack Exchange account, which burns it and credits an off-chain UCC Article 8 security entitlement.

Real SpaceX shares are held through regulated US brokerage infrastructure in an OMNIBUS account at RQD Clearing, LLC (Clearing Broker; SEC-registered, FINRA & SIPC member, CRD 134284 / SEC 8-66826), with Atomic Vaults Securities, LLC as Intermediary Broker (CRD 317194 / SEC 8-70868). Under the Issuer T&C the Underlying Assets are held by Trek Nexus Markets Ltd 'as legal owner or holder of record and as bare trustee', and the trustee 'may hold Underlying Assets and proceeds in omnibus or commingled accounts' (commingled only within the same Approved Asset pool) while simultaneously stating it 'does not act as a commercial custodian or administrator' and may appoint unnamed regulated custodians. NO custodian for the tokenized pool is named in any document, and how the BVI bare trust's legal title sits alongside the RQD/Atomic Vaults account chain is undocumented. SIPC: the Brokerage ToS states that stocks are held in the Omnibus Account and 'only the Omnibus Account will receive SIPC coverage', which 'may therefore be shared among all Users and may be insufficient'; and expressly 'The Tokens are not insured or guaranteed by SIPC, any deposit insurance scheme, or any governmental agency.' the Intermediary Broker is REGION-DEPENDENT and is not necessarily the SEC-registered firm the support pages name. The live product page carries a geo-dependent footer reading 'Brokerage services in your region are provided through Trek Brokerage Services Limited, a company licensed by the Anjouan Offshore Finance Authority, acting as Intermediary Broker pursuant to the Backpack Securities Brokerage Services Terms of Service.' The Brokerage ToS contemplates exactly that — 'Intermediary Broker' is defined as 'any Affiliate of Backpack Exchange that may act as an intermediary in the Brokerage Chain, as displayed on the Platform to certain Users from time to time' — but note what changes: Atomic Vaults Securities, LLC is a THIRD-PARTY SEC-registered broker-dealer holders are told to verify on BrokerCheck, while Trek Brokerage Services Limited is a Backpack AFFILIATE supervised in Anjouan (Comoros), and no reachable public Anjouan register exists to test the licence. Only the Clearing Broker is named in the binding terms ('RQD* Clearing, LLC'); the intermediary slot is filled by the Platform at its discretion.

links.label: Issuance and redemption

fields.value: Practically: any user with a KYC-verified Backpack Exchange account in a supported region (not US/UK/UAE/Japan, not Backpack EU) can deposit the token and have it converted into a traditional securities holding. Legally: only Trek Forge Ltd (or its nominee/custodian) may submit a redemption request to the trustee; 'on-chain holders and holders of Exchange Account Entitlements have no entitlement to access Redemption or burning functionalities in the ordinary course' (cl. 4.1(a)). Direct redemption against the trustee is available only after a Direct Redemption Contingency and then only subject to the trustee's KYC/KYT, proof of entitlement and express register update. No Prohibited Person or U.S. person may be registered as beneficiary or exercise redemption (cl. 4.1(c)).

Deposit the token from a Solana wallet into a Backpack Exchange account; the token is burned and the position becomes a traditional securities holding (a UCC Article 8 security entitlement) in the same account. The trustee's mechanics are: lock the tokens, burn them, then either transfer the pro rata portion of the pooled shares or — at the trustee's determination — sell them and relay the net cash proceeds ('Redemption Relay', cl. 4.2(iii)-(iv), cl. 4.6), so share delivery is not guaranteed. Onward movement to an outside broker is described as 'ACATS- and DTCC-eligible via the brokerage infrastructure', but Backpack's own support docs state plainly that 'ACATS transfers to other brokerages are still being worked on and are not currently available' and 'Support for external broker-to-broker stock transfers is still under development and is not yet available'.

Withdrawal of a tokenized security from Backpack Exchange to Solana: an estimated platform fee of approximately $0.50, paid in the tokenized security being withdrawn, with no additional fees. Deposits (token to traditional securities): no Backpack fee, holder pays the Solana network fee. Stock trading: no separate commission or platform fee; the quoted price is the traded price. Transaction Costs of a redemption are borne by the holder and netted from proceeds; the trustee may also set off amounts owing.

From Backpack's own asset API (https://api.backpack.exchange/api/v1/assets): minimumDeposit 0.004 SPCX, minimumWithdrawal 0.008 SPCX, withdrawalFee 0.004 SPCX. On the brokerage leg every stock order must be worth at least $1; fractional to 0.01 share during regular hours, whole shares only outside them.

links.label: Dividends and cash entitlements

fields.value: reinvested

For the token: dividends received on the pool are applied by the trustee 'to the acquisition of additional units of such Approved Asset (net of any applicable fees, expenses, or withholdings)' (cl. 3.7), and Backpack's marketing describes this as automatic reinvestment into additional tokenized shares with corporate actions reflected through 'proportional token balance adjustments designed to maintain economic equivalence'. the mechanism is a CONVERSION-RATIO change, not a balance adjustment. Asset Tokenization ToS s. 1.8 ('Conversion Rate') works a 25% distribution through as a Withdrawal Conversion Rate of 1:0.8 on the way in (s. 1.8(a)) and a Detokenization Conversion Rate of 1:1.25 on the way out (s. 1.8(b)) — the holder's token count never changes; what changes is how many units of the underlying each token detokenizes into, and fractions round DOWN to between two and six decimal places. The mint does carry the Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount extension that would perform a true rebase, and Issuer T&C cl. 1.2 builds 'token multiplier or rebasing ratios' into the Conversion Rate, so both routes are contemplated — but the multiplier has never moved: re-read 2026-09-18 it is multiplier '1', newMultiplier '1', newMultiplierEffectiveTimestamp 0, and SpaceX has paid no dividend and had no split. Backpack's own status table still lists corporate actions reflected in balances as 'still being worked on'. Voting: cl. 3.9 has the trustee exercise voting only on instructions from the registered Tokenholder — i.e. Trek Forge — so an on-chain holder has no voting channel; and on the off-chain brokerage side Backpack's own status table lists voting rights, cash dividend payouts, and splits/corporate actions reflected in balances as all 'still being worked on', not enabled.

links.label: Regulatory permission and disclosure

fields.value: The token side is unregulated and says so: 'The Company and the Tokens are not registered with, endorsed, or approved by the British Virgin Islands Financial Services Commission or any other regulatory authority', and the issuer asserts the Tokens 'do not constitute securities, certificates representing investments, depositary receipts, notes, collective investment scheme units, rights or interests in investments or other regulated investments as defined under the Securities and Investment Business Act (SIBA)'. The Risk Disclosure adds that Tokens 'are not designed or marketed as an investment product' and that nothing 'shall constitute an offer of securities or an investment, or be deemed to create an investment contract in any jurisdiction'. The distribution basis is Regulation S: the Asset Tokenization ToS states the Tokens 'have not been registered under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933 ... [and] may not be offered or sold in the United States or to US persons'. Regulated status sits one layer down, in the custody chain: RQD Clearing, LLC (Clearing Broker, CRD 134284 / SEC 8-66826) and Atomic Vaults Securities, LLC (Intermediary Broker, CRD 317194 / SEC 8-70868, formerly Olympus Mons Securities, LLC — note Backpack's docs spell it 'Atomic Vault' singular), both SEC-registered broker-dealers and FINRA & SIPC members. VERIFIED NEGATIVE: FINRA BrokerCheck firm search and SEC IAPD return zero records for 'Backpack', 'Backpack Securities', 'Trek Labs', 'Trek Nexus' and 'Trek Forge'; there is no CRD number, Form BD or SEC registration for any Backpack or Trek entity. SEC EDGAR full-text search returns no Backpack/Trek filings (the six hits for 'Backpack Securities' are unrelated third parties) and no Form D, Reg A or registration statement for SPCX. The consumer-facing introducing broker, Backpack Securities Global Limited, is a New Zealand corporation serving 'non-U.S. customers'. The widely repeated press description of SPCX as issued by 'a regulated U.S. broker-dealer' is therefore not supported by any primary document. Backpack Securities is NOT available to users in the United States, the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates or Japan, and is not offered on Backpack EU; cl. 4.1(b) prohibits transferring the token to or for the benefit of any U.S. person. Mark Wetjen (former CFTC Acting Chairman) was appointed President of 'Backpack US' around 2026-03-05, which signals a US expansion effort but is not itself a registration. STRONGEST NEGATIVE: Backpack's own 'US Licenses, Registrations, and Regulatory Disclosures' page, stated as current 'As of September 2026', discloses only money transmission — FinCEN MSB registration 31000329581307 for Trek Labs, Inc., NMLS ID 2665675, plus state money-transmitter licences (Delaware 042857, DC MTR2665675, Iowa 2025-0047 and others) — and contains zero occurrences of 'broker-dealer', 'FINRA', 'SEC' or 'Securities and Exchange'. That is the page a US broker-dealer registration would appear on. Separately, the Brokerage ToS says Backpack Securities Global Limited 'acts solely in its capacities as custodian of Stocks and as a Securities Intermediary'. Sector-wide regulator position: the SEC Division of Corporation Finance staff statement on tokenized securities (2026-01-28) distinguishes securities tokenized by or on behalf of the issuer from those tokenized by unaffiliated third parties, and holds that 'the format in which a security is issued or the methods by which holders are recorded (e.g., onchain vs. offchain) does not affect application of the federal securities laws'. SPCX is squarely third-party: SpaceX's own final prospectus (424B4, 2026-06-12, CIK 0001181412) contains zero occurrences of 'tokeniz', 'Solana' or 'Backpack', so the issuer of the underlying has neither endorsed nor acknowledged these tokens. MATERIAL QUALIFICATION 2026-09-18: even the one regulated layer is not the layer every user gets. The live SPCX product page footer states that in some regions brokerage services are provided through Trek Brokerage Services Limited, licensed by the Anjouan Offshore Finance Authority, as Intermediary Broker — a Backpack affiliate under Comoros supervision rather than the third-party SEC-registered Atomic Vaults Securities, LLC that the support pages tell holders to check on BrokerCheck. The Anjouan licence itself is UNVERIFIED: no reachable public AOFA register was found on 2026-09-18. Separately, the SEC engagement is now documented rather than inferred: a Crypto Task Force meeting memo records that on 2026-04-21 staff met representatives of Trek Labs, Inc. and Barbour, Griffith & Rogers — Can Sun (co-founder), Mark Wetjen (President of the Americas) and Keaghan Ames (BGR Group) — with an agenda covering CFTC DCM/DCO licensing and 'Securities Law Considerations and Potential SEC Oversight'. A Task Force meeting is a meeting, not a registration.

British Virgin Islands law governs the Issuer Terms and Conditions, and 'all transactions contemplated herein are deemed to occur in the British Virgin Islands' (cl. 2.1). New York law (UCC Article 8, incl. s.8-110(e)) governs the separate OFF-CHAIN security entitlement held in a Backpack Securities account. BVI Electronic Transactions Act 2001 is invoked for electronic assignment of beneficial interests.

conclusions.label: Position if an intermediary fails
conclusions.conclusion: The token is, in the issuer's own words, 'a non-negotiable digital record evidencing a pro rata beneficial entitlement (if any)' as beneficiary of a BVI bare trust over a pooled holding of the referenced shares — with no entitlement to any specific identifiable share. Crucially, the trustee recognises only Trek Forge Ltd (a Backpack affiliate) as Tokenholder and sole beneficiary; a person holding the token in their own wallet 'becomes the on-chain holder of those Tokens for blockchain transfer purposes only' and has no redemption, distribution, instruction or enforcement right against the trust unless and until a 'Direct Redemption Contingency' occurs (Backpack insolvency, cessation, >90 days of suspended redemptions, court order, etc.) and the trustee expressly registers them. In practice a holder realises value by depositing the token back into a KYC'd Backpack Exchange account, which burns it and credits an off-chain UCC Article 8 security entitlement.
conclusions.governingLaw: British Virgin Islands law governs the Issuer Terms and Conditions, and 'all transactions contemplated herein are deemed to occur in the British Virgin Islands' (cl. 2.1). New York law (UCC Article 8, incl. s.8-110(e)) governs the separate OFF-CHAIN security entitlement held in a Backpack Securities account. BVI Electronic Transactions Act 2001 is invoked for electronic assignment of beneficial interests.

conclusions.label: How value can leave the wrapper
conclusions.conclusion: Deposit the token from a Solana wallet into a Backpack Exchange account; the token is burned and the position becomes a traditional securities holding (a UCC Article 8 security entitlement) in the same account. The trustee's mechanics are: lock the tokens, burn them, then either transfer the pro rata portion of the pooled shares or — at the trustee's determination — sell them and relay the net cash proceeds ('Redemption Relay', cl. 4.2(iii)-(iv), cl. 4.6), so share delivery is not guaranteed. Onward movement to an outside broker is described as 'ACATS- and DTCC-eligible via the brokerage infrastructure', but Backpack's own support docs state plainly that 'ACATS transfers to other brokerages are still being worked on and are not currently available' and 'Support for external broker-to-broker stock transfers is still under development and is not yet available'.

conclusions.label: How shareholder economics pass through
conclusions.conclusion: For the token: dividends received on the pool are applied by the trustee 'to the acquisition of additional units of such Approved Asset (net of any applicable fees, expenses, or withholdings)' (cl. 3.7), and Backpack's marketing describes this as automatic reinvestment into additional tokenized shares with corporate actions reflected through 'proportional token balance adjustments designed to maintain economic equivalence'. the mechanism is a CONVERSION-RATIO change, not a balance adjustment. Asset Tokenization ToS s. 1.8 ('Conversion Rate') works a 25% distribution through as a Withdrawal Conversion Rate of 1:0.8 on the way in (s. 1.8(a)) and a Detokenization Conversion Rate of 1:1.25 on the way out (s. 1.8(b)) — the holder's token count never changes; what changes is how many units of the underlying each token detokenizes into, and fractions round DOWN to between two and six decimal places. The mint does carry the Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount extension that would perform a true rebase, and Issuer T&C cl. 1.2 builds 'token multiplier or rebasing ratios' into the Conversion Rate, so both routes are contemplated — but the multiplier has never moved: re-read 2026-09-18 it is multiplier '1', newMultiplier '1', newMultiplierEffectiveTimestamp 0, and SpaceX has paid no dividend and had no split. Backpack's own status table still lists corporate actions reflected in balances as 'still being worked on'. Voting: cl. 3.9 has the trustee exercise voting only on instructions from the registered Tokenholder — i.e. Trek Forge — so an on-chain holder has no voting channel; and on the off-chain brokerage side Backpack's own status table lists voting rights, cash dividend payouts, and splits/corporate actions reflected in balances as all 'still being worked on', not enabled.

sourceAuthority.rule: The conclusion follows the highest-authority source applicable to the specific product, holder and issue. A technical capability cannot create a legal right, and marketing cannot override operative terms.

scope.entityJurisdiction: British Virgin Islands (token issuer and the recognised beneficiary); New Zealand (Backpack Securities Global Limited, introducing broker for non-US customers); United States (RQD Clearing, LLC and Atomic Vaults Securities, LLC — the only SEC-registered brokers anywhere in the chain, both third parties; and Trek Labs, Inc., Delaware, a FinCEN MSB). Anjouan (Union of the Comoros) — the live SPCX page's geo-dependent footer names Trek Brokerage Services Limited, 'a company licensed by the Anjouan Offshore Finance Authority', as Intermediary Broker for some regions, so an offshore affiliate sits in the brokerage chain alongside the US firms. The New Zealand Companies Register confirms: Backpack Securities Global Limited is NZ company 9406953, NZBN 9429053463876, incorporated 25 Feb 2026, registered office 145 Ardmore Street, Wanaka — and it was named TREK LABS BROKERAGE SERVICES LIMITED from 19 Feb 2026 to 29 May 2026, i.e. renamed twelve days before the Issuer T&C's 2026-06-10 effective date. Incorporation is not licensing: the NZ Financial Service Providers Register could not be read (Incapsula block), so its FSP registration is unverified either way.
scope.governingLaw: British Virgin Islands law governs the Issuer Terms and Conditions, and 'all transactions contemplated herein are deemed to occur in the British Virgin Islands' (cl. 2.1). New York law (UCC Article 8, incl. s.8-110(e)) governs the separate OFF-CHAIN security entitlement held in a Backpack Securities account. BVI Electronic Transactions Act 2001 is invoked for electronic assignment of beneficial interests.

insolvency.headline: Insolvency outcome is not established.
insolvency.holderStanding: The token is, in the issuer's own words, 'a non-negotiable digital record evidencing a pro rata beneficial entitlement (if any)' as beneficiary of a BVI bare trust over a pooled holding of the referenced shares — with no entitlement to any specific identifiable share. Crucially, the trustee recognises only Trek Forge Ltd (a Backpack affiliate) as Tokenholder and sole beneficiary; a person holding the token in their own wallet 'becomes the on-chain holder of those Tokens for blockchain transfer purposes only' and has no redemption, distribution, instruction or enforcement right against the trust unless and until a 'Direct Redemption Contingency' occurs (Backpack insolvency, cessation, >90 days of suspended redemptions, court order, etc.) and the trustee expressly registers them. In practice a holder realises value by depositing the token back into a KYC'd Backpack Exchange account, which burns it and credits an off-chain UCC Article 8 security entitlement.

operationalDetails.segregationOrTrust: The token is, in the issuer's own words, 'a non-negotiable digital record evidencing a pro rata beneficial entitlement (if any)' as beneficiary of a BVI bare trust over a pooled holding of the referenced shares — with no entitlement to any specific identifiable share.
operationalDetails.omnibusOrCommingling: Real SpaceX shares are held through regulated US brokerage infrastructure in an OMNIBUS account at RQD Clearing, LLC (Clearing Broker; SEC-registered, FINRA & SIPC member, CRD 134284 / SEC 8-66826), with Atomic Vaults Securities, LLC as Intermediary Broker (CRD 317194 / SEC 8-70868).
operationalDetails.enforcementStanding: No separate enforcement representative is structured here; standing depends on the holder claim and governing terms reproduced above.

insolvency.caveat: A contractual label such as “segregated”, “trust” or “first priority” is not treated as a court-tested insolvency result unless the dossier records that authority.

corporateActions.actions: For the token: dividends received on the pool are applied by the trustee 'to the acquisition of additional units of such Approved Asset (net of any applicable fees, expenses, or withholdings)' (cl. 3.7), and Backpack's marketing describes this as automatic reinvestment into additional tokenized shares with corporate actions reflected through 'proportional token balance adjustments designed to maintain economic equivalence'. the mechanism is a CONVERSION-RATIO change, not a balance adjustment. Asset Tokenization ToS s. 1.8 ('Conversion Rate') works a 25% distribution through as a Withdrawal Conversion Rate of 1:0.8 on the way in (s. 1.8(a)) and a Detokenization Conversion Rate of 1:1.25 on the way out (s. 1.8(b)) — the holder's token count never changes; what changes is how many units of the underlying each token detokenizes into, and fractions round DOWN to between two and six decimal places. The mint does carry the Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount extension that would perform a true rebase, and Issuer T&C cl. 1.2 builds 'token multiplier or rebasing ratios' into the Conversion Rate, so both routes are contemplated — but the multiplier has never moved: re-read 2026-09-18 it is multiplier '1', newMultiplier '1', newMultiplierEffectiveTimestamp 0, and SpaceX has paid no dividend and had no split. Backpack's own status table still lists corporate actions reflected in balances as 'still being worked on'. Voting: cl. 3.9 has the trustee exercise voting only on instructions from the registered Tokenholder — i.e. Trek Forge — so an on-chain holder has no voting channel; and on the off-chain brokerage side Backpack's own status table lists voting rights, cash dividend payouts, and splits/corporate actions reflected in balances as all 'still being worked on', not enabled.
corporateActions.caveat: Economic equivalence may be delivered by cash, balance adjustment or issuer calculation; it is not assumed to reproduce the underlying shareholder right.

redemption.eligibility: Practically: any user with a KYC-verified Backpack Exchange account in a supported region (not US/UK/UAE/Japan, not Backpack EU) can deposit the token and have it converted into a traditional securities holding. Legally: only Trek Forge Ltd (or its nominee/custodian) may submit a redemption request to the trustee; 'on-chain holders and holders of Exchange Account Entitlements have no entitlement to access Redemption or burning functionalities in the ordinary course' (cl. 4.1(a)). Direct redemption against the trustee is available only after a Direct Redemption Contingency and then only subject to the trustee's KYC/KYT, proof of entitlement and express register update. No Prohibited Person or U.S. person may be registered as beneficiary or exercise redemption (cl. 4.1(c)).
redemption.rails: Deposit the token from a Solana wallet into a Backpack Exchange account; the token is burned and the position becomes a traditional securities holding (a UCC Article 8 security entitlement) in the same account. The trustee's mechanics are: lock the tokens, burn them, then either transfer the pro rata portion of the pooled shares or — at the trustee's determination — sell them and relay the net cash proceeds ('Redemption Relay', cl. 4.2(iii)-(iv), cl. 4.6), so share delivery is not guaranteed. Onward movement to an outside broker is described as 'ACATS- and DTCC-eligible via the brokerage infrastructure', but Backpack's own support docs state plainly that 'ACATS transfers to other brokerages are still being worked on and are not currently available' and 'Support for external broker-to-broker stock transfers is still under development and is not yet available'.
redemption.fees: Withdrawal of a tokenized security from Backpack Exchange to Solana: an estimated platform fee of approximately $0.50, paid in the tokenized security being withdrawn, with no additional fees. Deposits (token to traditional securities): no Backpack fee, holder pays the Solana network fee. Stock trading: no separate commission or platform fee; the quoted price is the traded price. Transaction Costs of a redemption are borne by the holder and netted from proceeds; the trustee may also set off amounts owing.
redemption.minimum: From Backpack's own asset API (https://api.backpack.exchange/api/v1/assets): minimumDeposit 0.004 SPCX, minimumWithdrawal 0.008 SPCX, withdrawalFee 0.004 SPCX. On the brokerage leg every stock order must be worth at least $1; fractional to 0.01 share during regular hours, whole shares only outside them.
redemption.evidenceLabel: A redemption process is documented, but no independently observed completed redemption is recorded.

openQuestions: RESOLVED as a negative, kept for the record: there is no SEC-registered or FINRA-member entity named 'Backpack Securities'. BrokerCheck and SEC IAPD return zero records for Backpack, Backpack Securities, Trek Labs, Trek Nexus and Trek Forge; EDGAR has no filings. The only US registrations in the group are the two third-party brokers (RQD, Atomic Vaults) and a FinCEN MSB for Trek Labs, Inc. (Delaware) — the MSB itself was not verified against FinCEN's registrant database.

Who operates Solana program FewRXXTzV2WwigvTQNsVanhEmCM9wzfNvoT1divNtbVH, whose PDAs hold the permanent-delegate, freeze, pause, metadata, hook and mint authorities, and who holds its single upgrade-authority key ERc1sdq7Lwb74kjuage5foTpavWKxdwXHUvqfg2JX5gz? The program is unidentified in every Backpack and Sunrise document, is unilaterally upgradeable, has no published audit, and carries no timelock or notice obligation (cl. 8.2: the Company 'may, but is not required to, provide notice'). A permanent delegate reachable through a unilaterally upgradeable program is the strongest possible authority on a Token-2022 mint.
Has the permanent delegate ever been exercised, and is any log of admin actions published? Nothing was found.

Is there any attestation, proof-of-reserve or auditor report tying the 43,248.128967 SPCX outstanding to SpaceX shares held? None was found. What is the actual share count in the pool, and where is it evidenced?

Where exactly does legal title to the shares sit? The Issuer T&C say Trek Nexus Markets Ltd is 'legal owner or holder of record' as bare trustee; Backpack's pages say custody is at RQD Clearing and Atomic Vault Securities. The account chain linking a BVI trustee to those US brokers is not documented, nor is which entity's name is on the account.

Is the declaration of trust dated 2026-06-06 (the 'Instrument') published anywhere? It is the document that actually creates the trust, it is cited as governing by both Backpack (Issuer T&C cl. 1.7) and Sunrise's own ToS, and it could not be found anywhere. Holders cannot read the instrument that defines their entitlement.

Terminology conflict inside Backpack's own materials: the tokenized-securities comparison table says the legal framework is a 'Claim on SPV holding the underlying assets', while the binding Issuer T&C describe a BVI bare trust, and the 'Real Ownership & Legal Framework' page boasts the product is 'not ... SPV interest'. Which characterisation does the issuer stand behind?

Backpack's docs spell the intermediary broker 'Atomic Vault Securities, LLC'; FINRA's registered name is 'Atomic Vaults Securities, LLC' (plural, formerly Olympus Mons Securities, LLC). A small inaccuracy, but it is in the one sentence holders are told to verify on BrokerCheck.

Has a Direct Redemption Contingency mechanism ever been tested, and what evidence of entitlement would the trustee accept from an on-chain holder? The Risk Disclosure says there is 'no guarantee... that the Company will accept your evidence of entitlement'.

When will ACATS/DTCC external transfers, cash dividends, corporate-action balance updates and voting actually go live? All four were still listed as 'being worked on' in docs updated around 2026-09-06, roughly three months after launch.

Does Backpack hold SPCX in Exchange Custody for users who never withdraw, and if so what is the split between exchange-held and self-custodied supply? That ratio determines how much of the 27,160 holder count actually has redemption rights.

Are the terms versioned? The Google Drive hosting means a silent amendment would leave no public trace, while cl. 2.4 binds every secondary acquirer to 'any amendments in effect at the time of such acquisition'.

The Risk Disclosure and the Terms and Conditions do not list the same Direct Redemption Contingencies. Risk Disclosure p. 4 tells holders the contingency "may include insolvency, delisting, prolonged suspension of Backpack Exchange, or other specified events outside your control", but Issuer T&C cl. 1.3 defines the term exhaustively as (a) permanent cessation of Backpack Exchange's operations or services, (b) its insolvency, (c) suspension of redemptions or withdrawals for a continuous period exceeding 90 days, (d) Trek Forge notifying the Company it will no longer act as sole recognised Tokenholder, (e) a final court order or binding regulatory directive, or (f) the Company's own reasonable determination that exclusive recognition of Trek Forge is no longer possible or appropriate. There is NO delisting limb. Does a delisting of the token (or of the underlying) trigger direct redemption via (a) or (f), or does it not trigger it at all? On the face of the binding document, a delisting alone does nothing.

Which users get which Intermediary Broker, and on what basis? The live SPCX page footer names Trek Brokerage Services Limited (Anjouan Offshore Finance Authority), the support pages name Atomic Vaults Securities, LLC (CRD 317194), and the Brokerage ToS leaves the slot to 'any Affiliate of Backpack Exchange ... as displayed on the Platform to certain Users from time to time'. Nothing published says which regions get which, whether the choice changes what SIPC or segregation protection applies, or whether Trek Brokerage Services Limited in fact holds an Anjouan licence — no reachable public AOFA register was found on 2026-09-18.

SPCX the Nasdaq ticker and SPCX the Solana token share a symbol, and Jupiter also lists Ondo's SPCXon, Backed's SPCXx, Tessera's tSpaceX and leveraged Shift wrappers. Is there any issuer guidance to prevent holders from depositing the wrong SPCX-symbol token to Backpack? The docs warn holders to verify the contract address but the collision is structural.

Why does Backpack's asset API publish 1,159 Solana contract addresses for .US instruments while only 56 have deposits and withdrawals enabled? Are the other 1,103 pre-created future mints, retired products, or an internal instrument universe, and what lifecycle signal besides the two enablement booleans should a holder rely on? Also: the enabled registry adds Backpack-issued USO and FWDI mints that the Jupiter-derived catalogue missed, while catalogue mint XYZ is no longer enabled and has zero on-chain supply.

The holder owns the actual ordinary share of the listed company. The 2026-08-12 press release furnished on Form 6-K states: 'These tokens are issuer-sponsored and recorded at the registry level, giving holders direct share ownership and the same legal standing as conventional shareholders - not a synthetic position or third-party wrapper.' The 2026-05-05 release: 'shareholders can now hold BLSH ordinary shares as tokens on the Solana blockchain' and 'Bringing real ordinary shares onto a public blockchain, administered by an SEC-registered transfer agent, is the next step.' There is no SPV, nominee or receipt layer. But the same release also states plainly that 'EQ maintains the official record of ownership whether shares are held in book-entry form or token form' — so the claim is a registered share recorded on EQ's register, of which the token is the on-chain representation.

None interposed. The token is the share; the register is EQ's. Shareholders 'withdraw, hold, and return tokens through EQ's Shareholder Central portal', i.e. the token form is a withdrawal of the shareholder's own registered position into a whitelisted wallet. No custodian, depositary or trustee is named for the tokenized form. Key management for the mint/freeze/permanent-delegate keys is undisclosed (contrast Superstate, which names Turnkey).

The route is now published: "If your shares are held at a broker, ask your broker to transfer your BLSH shares through the Direct Registration System (DRS) to Equiniti. Most major brokers can process DRS requests through customer support or a simple written instruction. Transfers typically settle within a few business days." After that there are two further gates: "To withdraw BLSH tokens, all shareholders must complete identity verification requirements" (KYC, or KYC/KYB for an existing login), and a wallet must be approved before it can receive - "Once approved, the wallet address is added to the BLSH token contract allowlist" - with withdrawal to a Bullish Exchange account as the alternative, "subject to Bullish’s jurisdictional availability and regulatory requirements". The register is not touched by any of it - "Your registered shares at Equiniti are not debited unless ownership of the shares is transferred". Bidirectional conversion between book-entry and token form via EQ's Shareholder Central portal: 'Shareholders can withdraw, hold, and return tokens through EQ's Shareholder Central portal.' No on-chain burn address is published, no SLA or expected duration is stated, and no cash payout results from returning tokens — the shareholder gets a book-entry position, which must then be sold through a broker on NYSE, or the token sold on Bullish Exchange.

fields.value: program-mediated — Token-2022 DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified on-chain 2026-09-16), so every newly created BLSH token account is born frozen and unusable until the freeze authority (single wallet 4Be7JXd6JaiXd6KkSMBEya5yt19gq1d11NEWTZC6Bsgk) thaws it. The issuer describes the effect exactly: 'Transfers of onchain BLSH today move bilaterally between EQ-whitelisted wallet addresses; AMM and DEX trading are not yet enabled. Any attempt to send BLSH tokens to a non-whitelisted address will fail at the smart-contract level, maintaining compliance with U.S. securities laws and anti-money-laundering rules.' Note a structural oddity: the mint carries an initialized TransferHook extension whose programId is null — the hook slot is reserved and its authority is the permanent-delegate wallet, but no hook program is set, so no per-transfer hook logic runs today. The gate is default-frozen accounts plus an off-chain-controlled freeze key, and the hook could be switched on later without redeploying the mint.

links.label: Dividends and cash entitlements

fields.value: none

Largely aspirational and entirely undocumented in operational terms. The 2026-05-05 release promises 'programmable corporate actions executed by smart contracts' as a possibility ('may open a set of possibilities'), not as a live feature. Dividends: Bullish has declared none on its ordinary shares, so there is no dividend path to test; no token dividend mechanism (cash, stablecoin or scrip) is described anywhere. Voting/proxy: a tokenized holder is a holder of record on EQ's register and should receive proxy materials through EQ's ordinary machinery, but no tokenized-holder proxy process is documented and there is no on-chain voting; no instance of a tokenized holder voting was found. Splits: the mint carries Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount with multiplier 1, so a split could be applied at the mint without reissuing tokens — never exercised. Emergency: the PausableConfig extension lets the authority halt all BLSH transfers in one instruction; no published policy governs when it would be used, who decides, or what holders are told. Lost/stolen shares: ANSWERED 2026-09-18, and the answer is no recovery. The PermanentDelegate makes it mechanically possible, but the issuer’s own risk-factors page now says the loss may be permanent - tokens sent to a lost, compromised or wrong address "may be permanently lost with no prospect of recovery by Bullish or any third party", and "We do not guarantee and may be unable to facilitate any replacement of or compensation for tokenized shares lost through key loss or wallet compromise." That supersedes the earlier "no recovery procedure is published": there is now a published position, and it is a refusal. NOTE THE INTERNAL CONFLICT on the same investor-relations site: the FAQ answers "What if I lose my wallet?" with "Contact Equiniti through Shareholder Central." - a support path with no stated remedy, evidentiary standard, fee or appeal - while the risk factor is the operative statement. What survives the token is the share: legal title sits in the register of members, which the same page calls "the definitive record of share ownership", and Equiniti carries the Rule 17Ad-17 lost-securityholder obligations.

links.label: Regulatory permission and disclosure

fields.value: Regulated US/Cayman/Gibraltar path with a documentary hole in the middle. The underlying security is the registered, NYSE-listed ordinary share of an SEC-reporting foreign private issuer. EQ is an SEC-registered transfer agent (File No. 084-00416). Bullish 'received approval from the GFSC to offer tokenized securities trading' in June 2026. The tokenization itself is disclosed to the SEC only by furnishing press releases on Form 6-K (2026-05-05 for the Equiniti merger, 2026-08-13 furnishing the 2026-08-12 tokenized-trading release); the tokenization is NOT described in the FY2025 20-F (filed 2026-03-10), which predates it and contains no mention of Equiniti (verified 2026-09-17: zero hits for 'equiniti' in the full document) or of tokenizing Bullish's own shares. The 20-F does, however, disclose the enabling registration twice - 'In December 2025, we registered with the SEC to operate as a transfer agent in the U.S.' (p. 45) and 'In December 2025, Bullish registered with the SEC as a transfer agent' (p. 49) - which is Bullish Digital TA LLC, SEC Transfer Agent File No. 084-07032, effective 2025-12-18, roughly five months before the launch. risk-factor disclosure DOES exist, though not in an SEC filing. Bullish publishes a dedicated "Risk Factors Relating to Tokenized $BLSH Shares" page on its investor-relations site, nine risk factors long, which supplies the tie-break between the chain and the register, the no-recovery position on lost keys, the reserved right to redeem or cancel tokens without holder consent, the sanctions-screening and eligibility conditions, and the tokenized-transfer tax hazard. It is not incorporated into any 20-F or 6-K, carries no SEC file stamp, and says of itself that it "may not reflect all risks associated with tokenized BLSH". No SEC no-action letter and no exemptive relief specific to Bullish was located; separately, on 2026-09-17 the SEC granted temporary conditional relief to Tokenized Securities Venues to trade tokenized NMS stock on permissioned AMM pools, which is the framework Bullish’s own FAQ says it is waiting for and which its GFSC-regulated venue sits outside. The 2026-05-05 release carries only a generic caution that 'Tokenized securities are a novel instrument and there is limited legal, regulatory, judicial, operational and market precedent for their treatment.'

Cayman Islands companies law governs the ordinary shares and the share register; US federal securities law governs the listing and the transfer agent (Exchange Act §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21 apply to EQ); Gibraltar financial services law governs the exchange that lists the token. NO token-specific terms of service, token holder agreement or governing-law clause for the tokenized form was located — this is the single largest documentary gap relative to the Superstate peer, where the Transfer Agent & Terms of Service Agreement and the Digital Transfer Agency Agreement are both public.

value.title: Bullish - "Risk Factors Relating to Tokenized $BLSH Shares" (investor-relations page, nine risk factors). THE most load-bearing document in this dossier and missing from the first two passes because the host answers curl and WebFetch with an Akamai 403 or a timeout while serving a node fetch with the watcher User-Agent. Uniquely establishes: the register-versus-chain tie-break ("the register of members ... is the definitive record of share ownership, and any inconsistency ... will be resolved by reference to the register of members"); that a lost key means the tokens "may be permanently lost with no prospect of recovery by Bullish or any third party", with no replacement or compensation; the reserved right to redeem, cancel, restrict or block without holder consent, "enabled by smart contract functionality such as administrative or operator controls embedded in the token code"; that holders may face sanctions screening and eligibility requirements, and that non-compliant holders’ wallets may be frozen or their tokens redeemed; the on-chain transfer as a possible taxable disposal; and the admission that a migration to a new contract address may be the only fix for a contract defect.

NOT FOUND, and the central documentary gap: no token terms of service, holder agreement, digital transfer agency agreement, whitepaper, technical documentation, allowlist policy, fee schedule or smart-contract audit for onchain BLSH was located anywhere. The Superstate peer publishes all of these.

Bullish investor-relations page "Tokenized $BLSH Shares" - the withdrawal process and FAQ, and the only published operational account of the conversion. Uniquely establishes the street-name pathway (a DRS transfer to Equiniti, "typically settle within a few business days"), the identity-verification gate, the wallet-approval step ("Once approved, the wallet address is added to the BLSH token contract allowlist"), the Bullish Exchange alternative "subject to Bullish's jurisdictional availability and regulatory requirements", the first published sanctions-screening commitment (OFAC and similar deny lists cannot be whitelisted), the answer "Contact Equiniti through Shareholder Central." to losing a wallet, and the statements that no US broker-dealer serves tokenized BLSH and that DEX trading awaits an SEC framework.

Bullish final IPO prospectus, Form 424(b)(4) filed 2025-08-13 - cited throughout this dossier and previously absent from documents[] and sources[]. The only source for the share's own terms: one vote per ordinary share, registered form with no bearer shares, the winding-up distribution rule, amendment of the articles by special resolution, the Cayman statutory rule that the register of members confers legal title with rectification by the Grand Court, the merger and squeeze-out mechanics and the absence of appraisal rights in a scheme of arrangement, Cayman taxation, and counsel's note that no class action has been reported in a Cayman court.

Bullish GI Exchange Terms of Service (23 June 2026), PDF - the venue contract, and the only document that describes what happens to a tokenized asset held on the exchange. Uniquely establishes: 5.3, the holder acknowledges an issuer "may have the technical and/or legal ability to freeze, seize, or modify the ownership of its Tokenized Assets" and Bullish "will comply with verified instructions from an Issuer"; 12.4-12.5, custody as bare trustee in segregated omnibus wallets with only an unsecured claim against a failed sub-custodian; 13.11, no Gibraltar Investor Compensation Scheme cover because the venue serves only professional clients; 4.10, the delisting grounds; 28.4, corporate actions passed through on commercially reasonable endeavours by rebasing or extra units; 28.5, no voting facilitation for tokenized assets; 40, Gibraltar law and LCIA arbitration in London.

Bullish Markets Rules (24 June 2026), PDF - the market rulebook, and the bluntest published statement of consequence anywhere in the Bullish record: 69.2, an issuer may "freeze, seize, modify, or permanently destroy ('burn')" its tokenized assets, the Operator as custodian may be obliged to comply, "The exercise of such controls by an Issuer may result in the partial or total loss of a Participant's assets without prior notice from the Operators", and the Operators "shall not be liable for any Losses" arising from complying. Also 14.1-14.5 on suspension and removal (including the underlying being delisted from its primary exchange) and 61 on forks and voting rights.

Bullish GI Trading Rules (25 June 2026), PDF - the order-handling and auction rulebook for the venue on which tokenized BLSH trades; the fourth of the four Gibraltar rulebooks and the one that governs how an order becomes a trade, including the Bullish Closing Cross auction mechanics referenced in this dossier's pricing notes.

Bullish GI Risk Warnings (23 June 2026), PDF - the venue's risk disclosure, and the source of the one sentence that bounds the exit: "Bullish will not facilitate any option for a holder of a Tokenized Asset to redeem it for the Underlying Asset via the Bullish Exchange; holders of Tokenized Assets may be able to redeem directly with the Issuer after the Tokenized Asset has been transferred to an external wallet which has been approved by the relevant Issuer." Also disclaims liability for an issuer's fraud, malfeasance or negligence.

Bullish Gibraltar legal hub - the index page from which the four June 2026 rulebooks are served, and the way to detect a new version: the PDF URLs are content-hashed, so a replaced rulebook gets a new URL and the old one is not updated in place.

SEC order In the Matter of Equiniti Trust Company, LLC f/k/a American Stock Transfer & Trust Company, LLC, Exchange Act Release No. 100780 (20 August 2024), PDF - a decided regulatory case against the very firm that keeps the BLSH register, and the only precedent in this stack for the register layer being manipulated. Establishes that a threat actor impersonating an issuer contact caused millions of an issuer's shares to be issued, liquidated and wired abroad; that the transfer agent reimbursed the issuer and the affected accountholders in full; and that it was censured, ordered to cease and desist from violating Exchange Act §17A(d) and Rule 17Ad-12, and fined $850,000, with its registration left intact.

SEC press release 2026-90 (17 September 2026) - "SEC Issues 'Innovation Exemption' to Facilitate the Trading of Tokenized NMS Stock and Request for Comment". The framework Bullish's own FAQ says it is waiting for, and the conditions it would have to meet: same rights and privileges as the equivalent traditional class, smart contracts "auditable, public, and deployed on a public, permissionless distributed ledger", written notice to the issuer for third-party tokenizations, and a halt in the tokenized stock concurrent with any halt in the underlying on its primary listing exchange. Temporary, expiring five years after publication.

conclusions.label: What the holder owns
conclusions.conclusion: The holder owns the actual ordinary share of the listed company. The 2026-08-12 press release furnished on Form 6-K states: 'These tokens are issuer-sponsored and recorded at the registry level, giving holders direct share ownership and the same legal standing as conventional shareholders - not a synthetic position or third-party wrapper.' The 2026-05-05 release: 'shareholders can now hold BLSH ordinary shares as tokens on the Solana blockchain' and 'Bringing real ordinary shares onto a public blockchain, administered by an SEC-registered transfer agent, is the next step.' There is no SPV, nominee or receipt layer. But the same release also states plainly that 'EQ maintains the official record of ownership whether shares are held in book-entry form or token form' — so the claim is a registered share recorded on EQ's register, of which the token is the on-chain representation.

conclusions.conclusion: program-mediated — Token-2022 DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified on-chain 2026-09-16), so every newly created BLSH token account is born frozen and unusable until the freeze authority (single wallet 4Be7JXd6JaiXd6KkSMBEya5yt19gq1d11NEWTZC6Bsgk) thaws it. The issuer describes the effect exactly: 'Transfers of onchain BLSH today move bilaterally between EQ-whitelisted wallet addresses; AMM and DEX trading are not yet enabled. Any attempt to send BLSH tokens to a non-whitelisted address will fail at the smart-contract level, maintaining compliance with U.S. securities laws and anti-money-laundering rules.' Note a structural oddity: the mint carries an initialized TransferHook extension whose programId is null — the hook slot is reserved and its authority is the permanent-delegate wallet, but no hook program is set, so no per-transfer hook logic runs today. The gate is default-frozen accounts plus an off-chain-controlled freeze key, and the hook could be switched on later without redeploying the mint.

conclusions.label: How shareholder economics pass through
conclusions.conclusion: Largely aspirational and entirely undocumented in operational terms. The 2026-05-05 release promises 'programmable corporate actions executed by smart contracts' as a possibility ('may open a set of possibilities'), not as a live feature. Dividends: Bullish has declared none on its ordinary shares, so there is no dividend path to test; no token dividend mechanism (cash, stablecoin or scrip) is described anywhere. Voting/proxy: a tokenized holder is a holder of record on EQ's register and should receive proxy materials through EQ's ordinary machinery, but no tokenized-holder proxy process is documented and there is no on-chain voting; no instance of a tokenized holder voting was found. Splits: the mint carries Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount with multiplier 1, so a split could be applied at the mint without reissuing tokens — never exercised. Emergency: the PausableConfig extension lets the authority halt all BLSH transfers in one instruction; no published policy governs when it would be used, who decides, or what holders are told. Lost/stolen shares: ANSWERED 2026-09-18, and the answer is no recovery. The PermanentDelegate makes it mechanically possible, but the issuer’s own risk-factors page now says the loss may be permanent - tokens sent to a lost, compromised or wrong address "may be permanently lost with no prospect of recovery by Bullish or any third party", and "We do not guarantee and may be unable to facilitate any replacement of or compensation for tokenized shares lost through key loss or wallet compromise." That supersedes the earlier "no recovery procedure is published": there is now a published position, and it is a refusal. NOTE THE INTERNAL CONFLICT on the same investor-relations site: the FAQ answers "What if I lose my wallet?" with "Contact Equiniti through Shareholder Central." - a support path with no stated remedy, evidentiary standard, fee or appeal - while the risk factor is the operative statement. What survives the token is the share: legal title sits in the register of members, which the same page calls "the definitive record of share ownership", and Equiniti carries the Rule 17Ad-17 lost-securityholder obligations.

NO token-specific terms of service, token holder agreement or governing-law clause for the tokenized form was located — this is the single largest documentary gap relative to the Superstate peer, where the Transfer Agent & Terms of Service Agreement and the Digital Transfer Agency Agreement are both public.

precedence.label: Mandatory law, court orders and official registers

precedence.label: Product-specific final terms and operative agreements
precedence.rule: The document governing this product or series controls over a general description, subject to mandatory law.

precedence.label: Base prospectus and binding programme terms
precedence.rule: These govern the programme except where valid product-specific terms supplement or disapply them.

precedence.label: On-chain state
precedence.rule: Authoritative for what the program and current keys can technically do, but not by itself for legal ownership or enforceability.

precedence.label: Official operating documentation and attestations
precedence.rule: Evidence of process or reserves; it cannot silently enlarge rights excluded by the controlling legal documents.

precedence.label: Marketing, press and third-party descriptions
precedence.rule: Useful context only. A conflict is resolved in favour of the higher-authority source and remains visibly recorded.

sources.title: Bullish GI Exchange Terms of Service (23 June 2026), PDF - the venue contract, and the only document that describes what happens to a tokenized asset held on the exchange. Uniquely establishes: 5.3, the holder acknowledges an issuer "may have the technical and/or legal ability to freeze, seize, or modify the ownership of its Tokenized Assets" and Bullish "will comply with verified instructions from an Issuer"; 12.4-12.5, custody as bare trustee in segregated omnibus wallets with only an unsecured claim against a failed sub-custodian; 13.11, no Gibraltar Investor Compensation Scheme cover because the venue serves only professional clients; 4.10, the delisting grounds; 28.4, corporate actions passed through on commercially reasonable endeavours by rebasing or extra units; 28.5, no voting facilitation for tokenized assets; 40, Gibraltar law and LCIA arbitration in London.

Bullish GI Risk Warnings (23 June 2026), PDF - the venue's risk disclosure, and the source of the one sentence that bounds the exit: "Bullish will not facilitate any option for a holder of a Tokenized Asset to redeem it for the Underlying Asset via the Bullish Exchange; holders of Tokenized Assets may be able to redeem directly with the Issuer after the Tokenized Asset has been transferred to an external wallet which has been approved by the relevant Issuer." Also disclaims liability for an issuer's fraud, malfeasance or negligence.

Bullish GI Trading Rules (25 June 2026), PDF - the order-handling and auction rulebook for the venue on which tokenized BLSH trades; the fourth of the four Gibraltar rulebooks and the one that governs how an order becomes a trade, including the Bullish Closing Cross auction mechanics referenced in this dossier's pricing notes.

Bullish Gibraltar legal hub - the index page from which the four June 2026 rulebooks are served, and the way to detect a new version: the PDF URLs are content-hashed, so a replaced rulebook gets a new URL and the old one is not updated in place.

Bullish Markets Rules (24 June 2026), PDF - the market rulebook, and the bluntest published statement of consequence anywhere in the Bullish record: 69.2, an issuer may "freeze, seize, modify, or permanently destroy ('burn')" its tokenized assets, the Operator as custodian may be obliged to comply, "The exercise of such controls by an Issuer may result in the partial or total loss of a Participant's assets without prior notice from the Operators", and the Operators "shall not be liable for any Losses" arising from complying. Also 14.1-14.5 on suspension and removal (including the underlying being delisted from its primary exchange) and 61 on forks and voting rights.

NOT FOUND, and the central documentary gap: no token terms of service, holder agreement, digital transfer agency agreement, whitepaper, technical documentation, allowlist policy, fee schedule or smart-contract audit for onchain BLSH was located anywhere. The Superstate peer publishes all of these.

Bullish Form 6-K furnished 2026-08-13, Exhibit 99.1 — press release 'Bullish launches tokenized equity trading' dated 2026-08-12. SEC-filed source for 'issuer-sponsored and recorded at the registry level, giving holders direct share ownership ... not a synthetic position or third-party wrapper', for the GFSC approval in June 2026, and for the May 2026 cap-table tokenization.

Bullish Form 20-F for FY2025, filed 2026-03-10 — source for 150,833,916 ordinary shares outstanding at 2025-12-31. Contains NO mention of Equiniti and no risk factor on tokenizing Bullish's own shares (it predates the launch).

Bullish final IPO prospectus, Form 424(b)(4) filed 2025-08-13 - cited throughout this dossier and previously absent from documents[] and sources[]. The only source for the share's own terms: one vote per ordinary share, registered form with no bearer shares, the winding-up distribution rule, amendment of the articles by special resolution, the Cayman statutory rule that the register of members confers legal title with rectification by the Grand Court, the merger and squeeze-out mechanics and the absence of appraisal rights in a scheme of arrangement, Cayman taxation, and counsel's note that no class action has been reported in a Cayman court.

Bullish Digital TA LLC Form TA-1, filed 2025-11-18 — SEC Transfer Agent File No. 084-07032, CIK 0002096796, the group's OWN SEC-registered transfer agent. Registration effective per EFFECT 2025-12-18; annual TA-2 filed 2026-03-31. Item 8(a) names Bullish US Holdings LLC as sole member. Named in neither press release.

Equiniti Trust Company, LLC SEC transfer-agent registration filings (TA-1/A 2026-07-31, TA-2 2026-03-31, TA-1/A 2026-05-28, TA-1/A 2026-02-17), SEC File No. 084-00416, CIK 0000005876, formerly American Stock Transfer & Trust Company, LLC

Bullish Form 6-K furnished 2026-05-05 — Equiniti merger agreement dated 2026-05-04, ~$4.2bn in newly-issued Bullish ordinary shares at a 30-day pre-signing VWAP of $38.4797, closing expected Q1 2027, termination date 2027-02-04 (extendable to 2027-05-04 and 2027-08-04). Establishes that EQ is still an independent third party today.
Bullish Form 6-K furnished 2026-05-05 (second) — transcript of the 2026-05-05 investor call on the Equiniti acquisition

SEC order In the Matter of Equiniti Trust Company, LLC f/k/a American Stock Transfer & Trust Company, LLC, Exchange Act Release No. 100780 (20 August 2024), PDF - a decided regulatory case against the very firm that keeps the BLSH register, and the only precedent in this stack for the register layer being manipulated. Establishes that a threat actor impersonating an issuer contact caused millions of an issuer's shares to be issued, liquidated and wired abroad; that the transfer agent reimbursed the issuer and the affected accountholders in full; and that it was censured, ordered to cease and desist from violating Exchange Act §17A(d) and Rule 17Ad-12, and fined $850,000, with its registration left intact.

SEC press release 2026-90 (17 September 2026) - "SEC Issues 'Innovation Exemption' to Facilitate the Trading of Tokenized NMS Stock and Request for Comment". The framework Bullish's own FAQ says it is waiting for, and the conditions it would have to meet: same rights and privileges as the equivalent traditional class, smart contracts "auditable, public, and deployed on a public, permissionless distributed ledger", written notice to the issuer for third-party tokenizations, and a halt in the tokenized stock concurrent with any halt in the underlying on its primary listing exchange. Temporary, expiring five years after publication.

Bullish investor-relations page "Tokenized $BLSH Shares" - the withdrawal process and FAQ, and the only published operational account of the conversion. Uniquely establishes the street-name pathway (a DRS transfer to Equiniti, "typically settle within a few business days"), the identity-verification gate, the wallet-approval step ("Once approved, the wallet address is added to the BLSH token contract allowlist"), the Bullish Exchange alternative "subject to Bullish's jurisdictional availability and regulatory requirements", the first published sanctions-screening commitment (OFAC and similar deny lists cannot be whitelisted), the answer "Contact Equiniti through Shareholder Central." to losing a wallet, and the statements that no US broker-dealer serves tokenized BLSH and that DEX trading awaits an SEC framework.

Bullish - "Risk Factors Relating to Tokenized $BLSH Shares" (investor-relations page, nine risk factors). THE most load-bearing document in this dossier and missing from the first two passes because the host answers curl and WebFetch with an Akamai 403 or a timeout while serving a node fetch with the watcher User-Agent. Uniquely establishes: the register-versus-chain tie-break ("the register of members ... is the definitive record of share ownership, and any inconsistency ... will be resolved by reference to the register of members"); that a lost key means the tokens "may be permanently lost with no prospect of recovery by Bullish or any third party", with no replacement or compensation; the reserved right to redeem, cancel, restrict or block without holder consent, "enabled by smart contract functionality such as administrative or operator controls embedded in the token code"; that holders may face sanctions screening and eligibility requirements, and that non-compliant holders’ wallets may be frozen or their tokens redeemed; the on-chain transfer as a possible taxable disposal; and the admission that a migration to a new contract address may be the only fix for a contract defect.
BLSH token metadata document referenced by the mint's TokenMetadata extension — resolves, but carries only name, symbol, description and image; no CUSIP/ISIN, no register link, no attestation

Bullish investor-relations page for tokenized BLSH shares (stock-info path) - READABLE, correcting the earlier "was not readable from this host ... content unverified". On 2026-09-18 it redirects to investors.bullish.com/stock/tokenized-blsh-shares and serves HTTP 200 to a node fetch with the watcher User-Agent; the 403 and the timeout were artefacts of curl and WebFetch. Kept as a separate entry because it is the URL the dossier and the source registry already cite.

Bullish launch release, 2026-05-05 — 'Bullish tokenizes its shares, bringing BLSH onchain'. THE definitive primary document: publishes the mint address, names EQ as SEC-registered transfer agent, states EQ maintains the official record, and states the EQ-whitelisted transfer rule.

sourceAuthority.rule: The conclusion follows the highest-authority source applicable to the specific product, holder and issue. A technical capability cannot create a legal right, and marketing cannot override operative terms.

scope.entityJurisdiction: Cayman Islands (issuer, incorporation state code 'E9' in EDGAR). Transfer agent is a US entity regulated by the SEC. Trading venue is Gibraltar (GFSC). Shares are registered under the US Securities Act (F-1 effective 2025, 424B4 filed 2025-08-13) and listed on NYSE.
scope.governingLaw: Cayman Islands companies law governs the ordinary shares and the share register; US federal securities law governs the listing and the transfer agent (Exchange Act §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21 apply to EQ); Gibraltar financial services law governs the exchange that lists the token. NO token-specific terms of service, token holder agreement or governing-law clause for the tokenized form was located — this is the single largest documentary gap relative to the Superstate peer, where the Transfer Agent & Terms of Service Agreement and the Digital Transfer Agency Agreement are both public.

eligibleHolders.name: allowlisted wallets
eligibleHolders.note: ‘Transfers of onchain BLSH today move bilaterally between EQ-whitelisted wallet addresses ... Any attempt to send BLSH tokens to a non-whitelisted address will fail at the smart-contract level.’ Enforced by defaultAccountState=Frozen; unlike Superstate there is no allowlist program, so the permitted set cannot be enumerated by anyone outside EQ.

eligibleHolders.name: KYC-verified platform users
eligibleHolders.note: Moving between book-entry and token form requires an EQ Shareholder Central account. No eligibility criteria, jurisdictional exclusions, street-name pathway, KYC provider or refusal process is published.

transfer.mechanism: program-mediated — Token-2022 DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified on-chain 2026-09-16), so every newly created BLSH token account is born frozen and unusable until the freeze authority (single wallet 4Be7JXd6JaiXd6KkSMBEya5yt19gq1d11NEWTZC6Bsgk) thaws it. The issuer describes the effect exactly: 'Transfers of onchain BLSH today move bilaterally between EQ-whitelisted wallet addresses; AMM and DEX trading are not yet enabled. Any attempt to send BLSH tokens to a non-whitelisted address will fail at the smart-contract level, maintaining compliance with U.S. securities laws and anti-money-laundering rules.' Note a structural oddity: the mint carries an initialized TransferHook extension whose programId is null — the hook slot is reserved and its authority is the permanent-delegate wallet, but no hook program is set, so no per-transfer hook logic runs today. The gate is default-frozen accounts plus an off-chain-controlled freeze key, and the hook could be switched on later without redeploying the mint.

scope.distinction: A wallet may be technically able to receive a token while its owner is contractually ineligible, unable to redeem, or excluded from rights under the governing documents.

insolvency.headline: The holder claim is the registered share itself; transfer-agent and register continuity remain operational dependencies.
insolvency.holderStanding: The holder owns the actual ordinary share of the listed company. The 2026-08-12 press release furnished on Form 6-K states: 'These tokens are issuer-sponsored and recorded at the registry level, giving holders direct share ownership and the same legal standing as conventional shareholders - not a synthetic position or third-party wrapper.' The 2026-05-05 release: 'shareholders can now hold BLSH ordinary shares as tokens on the Solana blockchain' and 'Bringing real ordinary shares onto a public blockchain, administered by an SEC-registered transfer agent, is the next step.' There is no SPV, nominee or receipt layer. But the same release also states plainly that 'EQ maintains the official record of ownership whether shares are held in book-entry form or token form' — so the claim is a registered share recorded on EQ's register, of which the token is the on-chain representation.

operationalDetails.enforcementStanding: The person recognised on the official share register has shareholder standing; the token and transfer-agent process determine whether the wallet holder is that person.

insolvency.caveat: A contractual label such as “segregated”, “trust” or “first priority” is not treated as a court-tested insolvency result unless the dossier records that authority.

corporateActions.actions: Largely aspirational and entirely undocumented in operational terms. The 2026-05-05 release promises 'programmable corporate actions executed by smart contracts' as a possibility ('may open a set of possibilities'), not as a live feature. Dividends: Bullish has declared none on its ordinary shares, so there is no dividend path to test; no token dividend mechanism (cash, stablecoin or scrip) is described anywhere. Voting/proxy: a tokenized holder is a holder of record on EQ's register and should receive proxy materials through EQ's ordinary machinery, but no tokenized-holder proxy process is documented and there is no on-chain voting; no instance of a tokenized holder voting was found. Splits: the mint carries Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount with multiplier 1, so a split could be applied at the mint without reissuing tokens — never exercised. Emergency: the PausableConfig extension lets the authority halt all BLSH transfers in one instruction; no published policy governs when it would be used, who decides, or what holders are told. Lost/stolen shares: ANSWERED 2026-09-18, and the answer is no recovery. The PermanentDelegate makes it mechanically possible, but the issuer’s own risk-factors page now says the loss may be permanent - tokens sent to a lost, compromised or wrong address "may be permanently lost with no prospect of recovery by Bullish or any third party", and "We do not guarantee and may be unable to facilitate any replacement of or compensation for tokenized shares lost through key loss or wallet compromise." That supersedes the earlier "no recovery procedure is published": there is now a published position, and it is a refusal. NOTE THE INTERNAL CONFLICT on the same investor-relations site: the FAQ answers "What if I lose my wallet?" with "Contact Equiniti through Shareholder Central." - a support path with no stated remedy, evidentiary standard, fee or appeal - while the risk factor is the operative statement. What survives the token is the share: legal title sits in the register of members, which the same page calls "the definitive record of share ownership", and Equiniti carries the Rule 17Ad-17 lost-securityholder obligations.
corporateActions.caveat: Registration supports shareholder rights, but the operational channel for a token-held position must still be documented.

redemption.eligibility: Registered shareholders with an EQ Shareholder Central account, and - street-name holders too, by first becoming registered holders. The route is now published: "If your shares are held at a broker, ask your broker to transfer your BLSH shares through the Direct Registration System (DRS) to Equiniti. Most major brokers can process DRS requests through customer support or a simple written instruction. Transfers typically settle within a few business days." After that there are two further gates: "To withdraw BLSH tokens, all shareholders must complete identity verification requirements" (KYC, or KYC/KYB for an existing login), and a wallet must be approved before it can receive - "Once approved, the wallet address is added to the BLSH token contract allowlist" - with withdrawal to a Bullish Exchange account as the alternative, "subject to Bullish’s jurisdictional availability and regulatory requirements". Screening can refuse outright: "Persons on OFAC or similar deny lists, and addresses flagged as sanctioned or high-risk, cannot be whitelisted." The register is not touched by any of it - "Your registered shares at Equiniti are not debited unless ownership of the shares is transferred". STILL UNPUBLISHED: any fee schedule, minimum, turnaround or SLA for the token-to-book-entry leg, any refusal or appeal process, and any jurisdictional exclusion list.
redemption.rails: Bidirectional conversion between book-entry and token form via EQ's Shareholder Central portal: 'Shareholders can withdraw, hold, and return tokens through EQ's Shareholder Central portal.' No on-chain burn address is published, no SLA or expected duration is stated, and no cash payout results from returning tokens — the shareholder gets a book-entry position, which must then be sold through a broker on NYSE, or the token sold on Bullish Exchange.
redemption.fees: unknown — no fee schedule for tokenization, de-tokenization or wallet whitelisting was located.
redemption.evidenceLabel: A redemption process is documented, but no independently observed completed redemption is recorded.
