openQuestions: WHERE ARE THE TERMS? Still the central gap, and now sharper rather than softer. PARTLY ANSWERED (2026-09-18): the public record is no longer two press releases. Bullish publishes a nine-factor "Risk Factors Relating to Tokenized $BLSH Shares" page and a withdrawal-process and FAQ page on its investor-relations site, and the Gibraltar venue publishes four rulebooks (Exchange Terms of Service 23 June 2026, Markets Rules 24 June 2026, Trading Rules 25 June 2026, Risk Warnings 23 June 2026) that describe issuer freeze, seizure and burn powers over tokenized assets and the venue’s obligation to comply with issuer instructions. STILL NOT FOUND, and now positively implied to exist: the token’s own terms. The risk factors tell holders to "carefully review the terms and conditions applicable to the tokenized shares, including any provisions governing redemption, suspension, or cancellation, before investing" - a document nobody outside Bullish and EQ has seen. Also still missing: the transfer agency agreement, allowlist policy, fee schedule and any smart-contract audit. A direct request to Bullish IR for the EQ Shareholder Central tokenization terms remains the single highest-value next step. WATCHER NOTE: these IR pages are fetchable - investors.bullish.com answers curl and WebFetch with an Akamai 403 or a timeout, and answers a node fetch carrying the watcher’s own DEFAULT_USER_AGENT with HTTP 200 - which is how this was read on 2026-09-18.

ANSWERED (2026-09-18): the register of members controls, on the issuer’s own words. The risk-factors page states that "The register of members maintained by Bullish under applicable corporate law is the definitive record of share ownership, and any inconsistency between on-chain records and the register of members will be resolved by reference to the register of members." That is the single most useful sentence in the Bullish record for a holder, and it cuts both ways: a chain-side error cannot destroy your title, and the on-chain balance you can see is never the thing that decides. It also resolves the self-contradiction recorded in incidents for 2026-05-05 - the "single authoritative ledger" marketing loses to the register - and it is the legally necessary answer, since under the Cayman Companies Act the register confers legal title, with rectification available from the Grand Court. TWO THINGS THE ANSWER DOES NOT COVER, and they are what is left of this question: nothing says who bears a loss suffered in the interval before an inconsistency is resolved, and the same two documents now disagree about who maintains the register - the risk factor says Bullish, the launch release says EQ - which is exactly the question of who can freeze or claw back a position. No reconciliation report, attestation or register endpoint exists for anyone outside EQ to test the real-time-synchronisation claim.

Who holds the keys, Bullish or Equiniti? 4Be7JXd6... (mint + freeze) and DPT54eBQ... (permanent delegate, pause, hook, split, metadata, confidential transfer) are plain single-signer wallets with no multisig program account and no disclosed custodian. Whether the transfer agent or the issuer can freeze and claw back a shareholder's position is unresolved, and it is exactly the question the SEC transfer-agent rules would care about.

What is the real shareholder-level adoption? 151,810,063.5 tokens across 21 Token-2022 accounts. How much of that is a single DTC/Cede & Co. position or an EQ omnibus account, how many accounts are genuine shareholder self-custody wallets, and how many distinct shareholders have ever used Shareholder Central to withdraw? Without this, 'fully tokenized cap table' cannot be converted into a maturity signal. getTokenLargestAccounts on the mint was rate-limited (HTTP 429) on the public RPC on 2026-09-16 and should be retried against a paid endpoint — it would answer this in one call.

Why is a TransferHook extension initialized with programId null? The hook slot is reserved and its authority is the permanent-delegate wallet. Is a hook program planned (which would move compliance on-chain and make the perimeter auditable, a genuine upgrade), or is this an artefact of the mint-creation tooling? Either way a hook can be attached later with no notice.

Why is ConfidentialTransferMint configured at all, with autoApproveNewAccounts false and a null auditor ElGamal key? Confidential transfers on a security whose transfer agent must maintain a holder register is a strange combination. If confidential transfers were enabled with no auditor key, balances would be opaque to everyone including the transfer agent. Not enabled today; the configuration is unexplained.

When does the tokenization reach a risk factor? The FY2025 20-F (filed 2026-03-10) predates the launch and does not mention it. The FY2026 20-F, due around March 2027, is the first filing that must address tokenized BLSH in Item 3.D — and the Superstate issuers' disclosures ('no current trading venues', conversion 'could take up to multiple weeks', 'pricing discrepancies ... may be substantial') are the benchmark for what candid disclosure looks like.
What is the conversion latency between token form and NYSE-tradeable book-entry form? This is the number that bounds the basis between Bullish Exchange and NYSE. Unpublished.

What happens to the independence of the stack when the Equiniti acquisition closes (expected Q1 2027)? Today EQ is an independent SEC-registered transfer agent — the only outside party in the structure and the basis for much of what scores well here. Post-closing, issuer, transfer agent, tokenization infrastructure and trading venue are one group holding freeze, claw-back and pause keys over its own shareholders. Note also that the deal is not certain: the merger agreement can terminate if not consummated by 2027-02-04 (extendable to 2027-05-04 and 2027-08-04).

Is the tokenized form the same security identifier as the NYSE-listed share? No CUSIP or ISIN is published for either form and the token metadata carries none, so the same-class claim rests on the issuer's word plus the supply arithmetic. The Superstate peer's published CUSIPs are the sharpest wrapper-versus-share discriminator available and Bullish supplies no equivalent.

How do dividends, proxy voting and splits actually work for a token holder? Bullish pays no dividend, so the path is untested; ScaledUiAmount sits at multiplier 1, so no split has occurred; and 'programmable corporate actions executed by smart contracts' is offered as a possibility, not a mechanism. No tokenized holder is known to have voted.

ANSWERED (2026-09-18), and the answer is no. The risk-factors page states that tokens lost to a lost key, a compromised wallet or a send to a wrong address "may be permanently lost with no prospect of recovery by Bullish or any third party", that "blockchain-based transfers are generally irreversible", that holders "bear sole responsibility for the security of their wallets and private keys unless custody has been delegated to a regulated custodian that maintains independent recovery mechanisms", and that Bullish does "not guarantee and may be unable to facilitate any replacement of or compensation for tokenized shares lost through key loss or wallet compromise." THE CONFLICT TO CARRY FORWARD: the same investor-relations site answers "What if I lose my wallet?" with "Contact Equiniti through Shareholder Central." The risk factor is the operative statement; the FAQ offers a support path with no stated remedy, evidentiary standard, fee or appeal. Mechanically recovery remains possible - the permanent delegate can move or burn from any account without the holder’s signature, and defaultAccountState=frozen means a thief’s new address cannot receive unless EQ whitelists it - so this is a policy refusal, not a technical limit. Rule 17Ad-17 lost-securityholder obligations still bind EQ at the register layer, and the share itself survives in the register; what is unrecoverable is the token.

PARTLY ANSWERED (2026-09-18). The street-name half is answered: there IS a pathway, and it runs through the Direct Registration System. "If your shares are held at a broker, ask your broker to transfer your BLSH shares through the Direct Registration System (DRS) to Equiniti. Most major brokers can process DRS requests through customer support or a simple written instruction. Transfers typically settle within a few business days." So a street-name holder cannot obtain tokens as such - they must first become a registered holder - and then complete Shareholder Central identity verification and have a wallet approved onto the token contract allowlist. The jurisdictional half is NOT answered: no eligibility matrix and no excluded-jurisdiction list is published, screening can refuse a person on an OFAC or similar deny list or an address flagged as sanctioned or high-risk, and withdrawal to a Bullish Exchange account is "subject to Bullish’s jurisdictional availability and regulatory requirements" - which are unstated. For a NYSE-listed Cayman issuer whose register is roughly 80% non-US, that remains a live question, as does the absence of any fee, minimum or turnaround for the conversion.

DOES THE INNOVATION EXEMPTION REACH BULLISH? On 2026-09-17 the SEC granted temporary conditional exemptive relief to "Tokenized Securities Venues" from the Exchange Act definition of "exchange", to trade tokenized NMS stock on permissioned AMM liquidity pools, expiring five years after publication. Bullish’s own FAQ says it is waiting for exactly that framework ("We are engaging with the SEC on rules that would allow tokenized equities to trade on automated market makers and other decentralized venues"). But Bullish Exchange is GFSC-regulated and outside the relief, and two of the conditions cut against the current design: a TSV must verify that the tokenized stock "provides holders the same rights and privileges as does traditional NMS stock of an equivalent class", and its smart contracts must be "auditable, public, and deployed on a public, permissionless distributed ledger" - while Bullish publishes no audit, no token terms and no allowlist program. A third condition would be a real change to behaviour: a TSV "must stop trading in a tokenized NMS stock concurrently with any stoppage of trading in the underlying NMS stock on the primary listing exchange", and nothing today obliges Bullish Exchange to halt tokenized BLSH when NYSE halts BLSH. Whether Bullish seeks TSV status, for which entity, and what it would have to publish to qualify, is the thing to watch.

WHO HOLDS THE MINT AND FREEZE KEYS - and the register? The key question (openQuestions[2]) now has a documentary sibling rather than only an on-chain one. The risk-factors page says the register of members is "maintained by Bullish"; the launch release says "EQ maintains the official record of ownership whether shares are held in book-entry form or token form"; and the group holds a second SEC transfer-agent registration of its own (Bullish Digital TA LLC, 084-07032). The venue rulebooks make the stakes concrete: GI Exchange Terms of Service 5.3 has the holder acknowledge that "an Issuer may have the technical and/or legal ability to freeze, seize, or modify the ownership of its Tokenized Assets" and commits Bullish to "comply with verified instructions from an Issuer regarding such controls", and Markets Rules 69.2 adds that the exercise "may result in the partial or total loss of a Participant’s assets without prior notice" with no liability on the Operators. So three documents describe an issuer instruction being obeyed, and none of them says which entity in the group issues it or who signs for the keys.

links.label: Ownership of the underlying

fields.value: structured-note

The holder owns an unsecured-in-form but collateral-secured debt claim on Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited — a blockchain-based tracker certificate / structured note whose redemption amount tracks the total return of the referenced share or ETF. The holder has a put option to redeem for cash/stablecoin at the tracked value, plus the benefit of a first-priority perfected security interest in the collateral held by Ankura Trust Company as Security Agent; the holder has no shareholder voting or information rights. Physical delivery of the underlying is excluded under the Sales Terms and no party may demand conversion into certificated, uncertificated or book-entry securities — with one documented exception outside the Sales Terms: authorized participants with a linked Alpaca brokerage account can redeem Ondo Stocks for the underlying securities through Alpaca's Instant Tokenization Network (ITN) on Ethereum and BNB Chain.

Alpaca Securities LLC (SEC-registered, FINRA member broker-dealer; New York) holds the equities/ETFs through the DTC indirect holding system and provides the trading/clearing accounts. BitGo Trust Company, Inc. (Sioux Falls, SD) holds fiat and stablecoins/tokens. The 2026-09-10 Ankura report also names SVB, Coinbase, Circle, Anchorage and a 'Bridge Account' and 'PSM' as holding locations for cash/stablecoins.

links.label: Issuance and redemption

fields.value: Only 'Onboarded Purchasers' who have completed the issuer's full KYC and satisfy the eligibility criteria (non-US person, not a Prohibited Person, and in several jurisdictions professional/accredited-investor status). KYC is an express condition precedent to redemption, so a secondary-market buyer may hold a token it cannot redeem. Onboarding was institutional-only at the time of the Solana launch, with retail 'coming soon'.

On-chain atomic mint/redeem against USDon (the platform stablecoin), with USDC atomically swapped 1:1 to/from USDon via a stablecoin swapper (users are not whitelisted for that swap by default). Requires an off-chain signed attestation (secp256k1) from the Ondo GM API quoting price and amount, submitted to the on-chain program by a whitelisted address. For an ordinary Onboarded Purchaser redemption is for cash/stablecoin only, and the Sales Terms exclude physical delivery and bar any conversion into certificated, uncertificated or book-entry securities. Separately, Alpaca's Instant Tokenization Network lets authorized participants mint from, and redeem into, the underlying securities in a linked Alpaca brokerage account on Ethereum and BNB Chain (no Ondo fee for ITN mint/redeem). Bank wire redemption not supported.

Sales Terms define Purchaser Fees owed to the Issuer for issuance AND redemption of up to 0.1% of the market price of the Underlyings; no separate redemption fee is advertised in the docs, and Ondo also retains the spread between the quoted token price and the price at which it trades the underlying. Ondo charges no fee for mint/redeem through Alpaca's ITN channel. Investor pays gas. Dividends are reinvested net of 30% US withholding tax on the BVI issuer.

links.label: Dividends and cash entitlements

fields.value: reinvested

Voting: since 2026-04-28, via a Broadridge integration, tokenholders can express non-binding voting PREFERENCES to the issuer regarding the shares the issuer beneficially owns; the issuer has no legal obligation to follow them, and the holder has no shareholder voting right. Dividends are reinvested into the referenced stock net of withholding tax and expressed as an increase in the 'shares per token' multiplier; on Solana this is surfaced through the Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount extension, so the displayed balance grows rather than the price (NVDAon multiplier 1.0017152487959897, AAPLon 1.003376073740221, SPYon 1.0077209101501272, TSLAon 1.0 as read on-chain 2026-09-16). Stock splits are handled the same way. Trading is paused around ex-dividend dates (roughly 7:50-8:10pm ET the day before the ex-date) and halted for ETF distributions until the amount is known; assets enter a reduced-size 'limited' state around earnings. Halts are listed at status.ondo.finance. The issuer may replace the Underlying held as collateral, and may exercise an Issuer Call Option to terminate and redeem all (not part) of a token series after a Termination Notice.

links.label: Regulatory permission and disclosure

fields.value: Not a registered US offering. Tokens sold only outside the US under Regulation S; issuer not registered as an investment company under the 1940 Act. EU-facing: Base Prospectus for a 'Program for the issuance of tokenized Securities' approved by the Liechtenstein Financial Markets Authority on 11.11.2025 (valid to 11.11.2026), with per-asset Final Terms filed with the FMA and PRIIPs Key Information Documents; NVDAon carries ISIN VGG7001AAH73. Some assets carry an 'Admission to Trading Notice on Binance MTF in Abu Dhabi Global Market'. Ondo Finance Inc. filed a no-action request with SEC Trading & Markets on 2026-04-13 to tokenize the DTC security entitlements that collateralise OGM products (via its SEC-registered transfer agent Oasis Pro TA, LLC) — that request does not cover issuance of the OGM tokens themselves. Two pending or historical items. (1) A confidential SEC registration statement for Ondo Stocks was announced by Ondo on 2026-02-03 (blog datePublished 2026-02-03T15:15:00Z) which, once effective, on Ondo's own account "would make Ondo Stocks the first issuer of transferable tokenized stocks to be subject to the SEC's reporting requirements". Nothing published shows it has gone effective, so this is a pending and not currently effective. (2) The SEC is reported to have closed a multi-year investigation into Ondo Finance without charges — UNVERIFIED: no readable primary source was available, so the report remains undated; it concerned Ondo Finance Inc. and the ONDO token, not Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited or these tokens.

Swiss law governs the form/transfer/cancellation of the tokens as Ledger-Based Securities under arts. 973d et seqq. CO, and governs the Sales Terms (arbitration: Swiss Rules, seat Zurich, English). Collateral Agreement and Alpaca account control agreement: New York law. BitGo account control agreement: South Dakota law. Administrative Services Agreement: Delaware law. Base Prospectus approved under EU Prospectus Regulation by the Liechtenstein FMA.

conclusions.label: How shareholder economics pass through
conclusions.conclusion: Voting: since 2026-04-28, via a Broadridge integration, tokenholders can express non-binding voting PREFERENCES to the issuer regarding the shares the issuer beneficially owns; the issuer has no legal obligation to follow them, and the holder has no shareholder voting right. Dividends are reinvested into the referenced stock net of withholding tax and expressed as an increase in the 'shares per token' multiplier; on Solana this is surfaced through the Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount extension, so the displayed balance grows rather than the price (NVDAon multiplier 1.0017152487959897, AAPLon 1.003376073740221, SPYon 1.0077209101501272, TSLAon 1.0 as read on-chain 2026-09-16). Stock splits are handled the same way. Trading is paused around ex-dividend dates (roughly 7:50-8:10pm ET the day before the ex-date) and halted for ETF distributions until the amount is known; assets enter a reduced-size 'limited' state around earnings. Halts are listed at status.ondo.finance. The issuer may replace the Underlying held as collateral, and may exercise an Issuer Call Option to terminate and redeem all (not part) of a token series after a Termination Notice.

precedence.label: Mandatory law, court orders and official registers
precedence.rule: These can override private terms and determine legal title, perfection, insolvency priority or eligibility.

precedence.label: Product-specific final terms and operative agreements
precedence.rule: The document governing this product or series controls over a general description, subject to mandatory law.

precedence.label: Base prospectus and binding programme terms
precedence.rule: These govern the programme except where valid product-specific terms supplement or disapply them.

precedence.label: On-chain state
precedence.rule: Authoritative for what the program and current keys can technically do, but not by itself for legal ownership or enforceability.

precedence.label: Official operating documentation and attestations
precedence.rule: Evidence of process or reserves; it cannot silently enlarge rights excluded by the controlling legal documents.

precedence.label: Marketing, press and third-party descriptions
precedence.rule: Useful context only. A conflict is resolved in favour of the higher-authority source and remains visibly recorded.

insolvency.headline: The holder relies on a security package and its perfection, priority, collateral scope and enforcement machinery—not direct ownership of the shares.

securityInterest.holder: Ankura Trust Company, LLC as Security Agent, for the benefit of the Secured Parties (tokenholders)

insolvency.holderStanding: The holder owns an unsecured-in-form but collateral-secured debt claim on Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited — a blockchain-based tracker certificate / structured note whose redemption amount tracks the total return of the referenced share or ETF. The holder has a put option to redeem for cash/stablecoin at the tracked value, plus the benefit of a first-priority perfected security interest in the collateral held by Ankura Trust Company as Security Agent; the holder has no shareholder voting or information rights. Physical delivery of the underlying is excluded under the Sales Terms and no party may demand conversion into certificated, uncertificated or book-entry securities — with one documented exception outside the Sales Terms: authorized participants with a linked Alpaca brokerage account can redeem Ondo Stocks for the underlying securities through Alpaca's Instant Tokenization Network (ITN) on Ethereum and BNB Chain.

operationalDetails.perfectionOrPriority: The holder has a put option to redeem for cash/stablecoin at the tracked value, plus the benefit of a first-priority perfected security interest in the collateral held by Ankura Trust Company as Security Agent; the holder has no shareholder voting or information rights.
operationalDetails.enforcementStanding: Ankura Trust Company, LLC as Security Agent, for the benefit of the Secured Parties (tokenholders) is the recorded security holder or enforcement representative; the tokenholder depends on that agent and the operative security documents.

insolvency.caveat: A contractual label such as “segregated”, “trust” or “first priority” is not treated as a court-tested insolvency result unless the dossier records that authority.

corporateActions.actions: Voting: since 2026-04-28, via a Broadridge integration, tokenholders can express non-binding voting PREFERENCES to the issuer regarding the shares the issuer beneficially owns; the issuer has no legal obligation to follow them, and the holder has no shareholder voting right. Dividends are reinvested into the referenced stock net of withholding tax and expressed as an increase in the 'shares per token' multiplier; on Solana this is surfaced through the Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount extension, so the displayed balance grows rather than the price (NVDAon multiplier 1.0017152487959897, AAPLon 1.003376073740221, SPYon 1.0077209101501272, TSLAon 1.0 as read on-chain 2026-09-16). Stock splits are handled the same way. Trading is paused around ex-dividend dates (roughly 7:50-8:10pm ET the day before the ex-date) and halted for ETF distributions until the amount is known; assets enter a reduced-size 'limited' state around earnings. Halts are listed at status.ondo.finance. The issuer may replace the Underlying held as collateral, and may exercise an Issuer Call Option to terminate and redeem all (not part) of a token series after a Termination Notice.
corporateActions.caveat: Economic equivalence may be delivered by cash, balance adjustment or issuer calculation; it is not assumed to reproduce the underlying shareholder right.

redemption.eligibility: Only 'Onboarded Purchasers' who have completed the issuer's full KYC and satisfy the eligibility criteria (non-US person, not a Prohibited Person, and in several jurisdictions professional/accredited-investor status). KYC is an express condition precedent to redemption, so a secondary-market buyer may hold a token it cannot redeem. Onboarding was institutional-only at the time of the Solana launch, with retail 'coming soon'.
redemption.rails: On-chain atomic mint/redeem against USDon (the platform stablecoin), with USDC atomically swapped 1:1 to/from USDon via a stablecoin swapper (users are not whitelisted for that swap by default). Requires an off-chain signed attestation (secp256k1) from the Ondo GM API quoting price and amount, submitted to the on-chain program by a whitelisted address. For an ordinary Onboarded Purchaser redemption is for cash/stablecoin only, and the Sales Terms exclude physical delivery and bar any conversion into certificated, uncertificated or book-entry securities. Separately, Alpaca's Instant Tokenization Network lets authorized participants mint from, and redeem into, the underlying securities in a linked Alpaca brokerage account on Ethereum and BNB Chain (no Ondo fee for ITN mint/redeem). Bank wire redemption not supported.
redemption.fees: Sales Terms define Purchaser Fees owed to the Issuer for issuance AND redemption of up to 0.1% of the market price of the Underlyings; no separate redemption fee is advertised in the docs, and Ondo also retains the spread between the quoted token price and the price at which it trades the underlying. Ondo charges no fee for mint/redeem through Alpaca's ITN channel. Investor pays gas. Dividends are reinvested net of 30% US withholding tax on the BVI issuer.

operationalEvidence.basis: Ondo's current operating material says direct mint/redemption is available 24/5 for all assets and 24/7 for NVDAon, SPYon, CRCLon, TSLAon, QQQon and GOOGLon across Solana, Ethereum and BNB Chain. Current docs state instant USDon redemption and USDC redemption when swapper liquidity is sufficient. This is official availability evidence, not an independently observed completed redemption.

openQuestions: What is the numeric overcollateralisation factor for 'Other Collateral' per asset type? The Sales Terms say it is defined therein and varies, but the value was not located in the public text, and the daily report gives only a pooled Asset-to-Obligation Ratio (108.02% on 2026-09-10).

How much of the collateral is actually the underlying shares versus permitted substitutes (cash, unlisted instruments, crypto assets)? The daily report shows a large stablecoin and cash component (~$66m USDC/USDT plus ~$35m Alpaca cash) but does not label any of it as Standard vs Other Collateral for a given series.

Why are the Ankura reports not published at https://ondo.finance/global-markets as Sales Terms s.8.1(b) requires, and is the Dropbox folder considered contractual compliance? Also: is the 2-4 business day publication lag a process issue or a change in practice?

Will a TransferHook program be installed on the Solana mints, and if so what will it enforce? The hook authority is set and press describes hooks as the compliance mechanism, but programId is null today — installing one would silently convert unconditionalTransfers from yes to no.

Who beneficially controls Ondo's Squads members, its two direct Solana operational keys and its off-chain quote signer? The mint/scaled-UI/pause PDA and its programme are now resolved: root upgrade and role control is 4 of 7 with a two-hour timelock, operational mint/deploy is 4 of 6 with 15 minutes, freeze is 3 of 8, recovery/configuration is 4 of 7, whitelist administration is 2 of 6, and emergency pause is 1 of 9. Still unpublished are signer identities and custody/rotation policy, the owners of unilateral multiplier updater 5Azsc... and stock-reference-price setter 5NC6Q8..., and whether secp256k1 attestation signer 0xff2d04f6002c10eba702adafe2f43cac5996c477 uses HSM/MPC or one private key.

The NVDAon Final Terms (11.11.2025) name Ethereum Mainnet only as the Blockchain. Have FMA-filed Final Terms been supplemented to cover the Solana issuance (Jan 2026), and does the Base Prospectus Supplement of 04.05.2026 do that?

ANSWERED (2026-09-18): yes, published and dated, and the Solana program is covered — by three reports, none of them the Spearbit or Cyfrin ones. https://docs.ondo.finance/audits lists TEN reports under 'Ondo Stocks': February 2026 Cantina, December 2025 Zellic, two December 2025 Cantina, November 2025 Cantina, November 2025 FYEO, October 2025 Cantina, September 2025 FYEO, July 2025 Cyfrin and June 2025 Spearbit. Three carry Solana-specific reports: GM-Solana-Zellic-12-29-2025.pdf, GM-Solana-FYEO-11-05-2025.pdf and GM-Solana-FEYO-09-08-2025.pdf (the last filename misspells FYEO). The Zellic report was read for this pass: 'Ondo Global Markets Solana Application Security Assessment', dated December 29, 2025, target 'gm-solana', 94 pages, 2.4 person-weeks over 1.2 calendar weeks, program 'ondo-gm', version 77fb5bdd0d192c3e0849ed331d9c2228b5eaa202. One loose end: the repository it names, github.com/ondoprotocol/gm-solana, returns 404 from the GitHub API today, while the public github.com/ondoprotocol/global-markets-solana was created 2025-12-29 — the same date the report carries — so the audited tree and the published tree are not demonstrably the same code.
Is there an annual audited financial statement for Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited? The docs promise annual independent audits 'made available to investors' but none was found published.

Practical effect of the Prohibited-Persons clause: a secondary buyer can receive the token but 'shall have no rights under any Offering Documents'. Does the issuer track and act on this, and how would it treat a chain of transfers through an ineligible holder?
The 2026-04-13 SEC no-action request would put the collateral security entitlements on Ethereum via Oasis Pro TA. Has the SEC responded, and would that change the OGM holder's claim?

Broadridge voting-preference passthrough (live 2026-04-28): does it require KYC/onboarding, a minimum holding, or an Ondo account, and is it available to Solana holders? The issuer's discretion to disregard preferences is not quantified or reported on.

links.label: Regulatory permission and disclosure

fields.value: Unlicensed and self-disclaiming. Site disclaimer: "PreStocks is not a broker-dealer, investment advisor, exchange operator, transfer agent, custodian, virtual asset service provider, or similar regulated entity." No securities registration or exemption is cited; the ToS instead asserts "All blockchain transfers via the Services are secondary transfers effected outside the United States and are not primary offerings to U.S. persons" (Regulation S-style posture, but Reg S is never named).

British Virgin Islands law. ToS s.“Governing Law and Jurisdiction”: all matters and disputes "shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the internal laws of the British Virgin Islands". Note the BVI is simultaneously on the Prohibited Jurisdictions list. Disputes go to good-faith negotiation for 30 days, then binding arbitration under the London Court of International Arbitration Rules; seat London, England; sole arbitrator; English language; individual basis only (no class actions), with the courts of the British Virgin Islands taking exclusive jurisdiction over any claim for which the class-action waiver is held unenforceable. What is still missing is the counterparty, not the law: no issuing entity or jurisdiction of incorporation is named.

evidenceDetail.basis: The current OPENAI product page offers acquisition but publishes no redemption address, form, SLA, minimum or settlement procedure. The current FAQ points holders to on-chain sale; the Terms preserve only a discretionary request that creates no entitlement. A presently usable issuer route is therefore not established.

openQuestions: Who actually issues the tokens? No legal entity is named anywhere; "a distributed network of contributors" is not a counterparty a holder could sue, and the LCIA clause names no respondent.
Which holding entities hold the exposure, and in what form? Names are withheld as policy, so the 1:1 backing claim in the API description is unverifiable in principle, not just in practice.
Is ANTHROPIC exposure backed at all after Anthropic declared SPV transfers void under its transfer restrictions? The token still trades and the supply was never reduced.
Has any attestation report ever been produced to any holder on request, and at what cost?
Why was the OPENAI scaledUiAmount multiplier set to 1.4861347 on 2026-07-17 - a share split at OpenAI, a restatement of units per token, or a correction of over/under-collateralisation?

Who beneficially controls the five voting members and two initiate-only members of Squads multisig 53Ab3R...? The on-chain threshold is now resolved as 2 of 5 with no timelock, but PreStocks discloses neither member identities nor why two accounts can propose without voting or executing.

RESOLVED, kept for the record: the ToS last updated 2026-09-08 does elect a substantive law - the internal laws of the British Virgin Islands - with LCIA arbitration seated in London and BVI courts as the fallback forum. The BVI is also a Prohibited Jurisdiction under the same document. What remains unanswered is who the BVI-law counterparty is.

RESTATED (2026-09-18), not answered: the question is not why SPACEX trades about 21% below the issuer's own mark but why the dislocation runs BOTH ways at once — OPENAI +11.4% and NEURALINK +14.8% above the mark on the same read that has SPACEX -21.9% below it. A one-way friction (redemption gated, minting open, or the reverse) cannot produce both signs simultaneously, so either the mark is wrong for some names, the mint and redeem paths are both discretionary in practice, or the arbitrage described in the FAQ is not being performed at all. The FAQ describes the mechanism; nothing published evidences a single completed arbitrage.
xAI has a live product page in sitemap.xml but no API entry or mint - is it unlaunched, delisted, or was it withdrawn?

links.label: Ownership of the underlying

fields.value: registered-share

The holder owns the actual registered common share. The S-1 risk factor is unambiguous on two points at once: 'we enabled Tokenized SECZ, a natively tokenized version of our common stock. Tokenized SECZ is not a separate share class' and 'Tokenized SECZ provides an additional mechanism for investors to hold and transfer shares in the Company'. The issuer's own press release adds that this is an 'issuer-sponsored tokenization of the same common stock trading on the NYSE' and that 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions.' Holders may move between forms: 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ'. There is no SPV, receipt or nominee layer in the legal structure — but access runs through a broker-dealer's onboarding, so whether the holder is a registered holder of record in their own name or a customer of the broker-dealer is NOT established by any document located, and this is the central unresolved question for this issuer.

No custodian is interposed for the security itself — the token is the share and the register is Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC's master securityholder file. For its own corporate digital assets Securitize discloses self-custody via Fireblocks MPC ('enables us to retain exclusive control over the authorization of transactions without ever generating or storing a traditional private key'), and states that 'In the case of Securitize-issued tokenized securities held in self-custody utilizing Fireblocks infrastructure, Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent.' Investor-side custody may be self-custody (see transferRestrictions) or broker/custodian-held; the split is not disclosed.

links.label: Issuance and redemption

fields.value: Holders who have completed the broker-dealer onboarding: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer.' The issuer's press release adds that the tokenized form is for 'eligible U.S. investors' subject to 'onboarding, KYC/AML verification, jurisdictional eligibility checks'. Certain Avalanche holdings are additionally subject to business-combination lock-up agreements.

Bidirectional switching between forms is asserted in one subordinate clause: "holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ". Only the INBOUND leg is documented, and it is a coordination between two transfer agents rather than an internal book movement: the holder asks their broker to move the shares out of street name "through the Direct Registration System (DRS) or Deposit and Withdrawal at Custodian (DWAC) method" to Continental Stock Transfer (DRS & DWAC #7808); Continental then "records you as the registered owner of the shares" and issues a statement; and only "Once your shares are registered directly on the transfer agent's shareholder ledger" can they be converted into tokenized form and issued to a Securitize-registered wallet. Securitize warns that "Not all brokers support DRS transfers" and that broker fees vary. The OUTBOUND leg — de-tokenization back to the Continental book-entry position — has no published procedure, burn address, processing time or fee anywhere, and the unquantified switch latency is the constraint the S-1 itself blames for potential price discrepancies between the two forms.

fields.value: program-mediated, per-token whitelist. On-chain: Token-2022 DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified 2026-09-16), so every new SECZ token account is frozen at birth and only the freeze authority (8Twerer..., an apparent program PDA) can thaw it; plus PausableConfig for a global halt. Off-chain: the Securitize Connect API documents wallet whitelisting scoped to a specific token ('adds a wallet address to the whitelist of an specific token', requiring a tokenId, since 'in a given domain there may be multiple tokens'), with wallet statuses 'ready, pending, failed' and a 'not-authorised' response state. Notably the whitelist is NOT tied to a platform-hosted wallet: 'This is not required, as the whitelisting at token level does NOT require the wallet being registered at Securitize iD' — a self-custodied address can be whitelisted directly. Contractually: 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions', and specific Avalanche holdings carry business-combination lock-ups. US persons are the TARGET market here ('eligible U.S. investors'), which inverts the usual tokenized-equity geofence.

links.label: Dividends and cash entitlements

fields.value: none

Securitize markets corporate-action servicing as a core transfer-agent capability — the S-1 describes 'a comprehensive suite of securities services including real-time approval, record-keeping, distributions, dividend issuances and compliance solutions' — so the institutional machinery genuinely exists and is exercised for third-party issuers (BUIDL and others). For SECZ specifically nothing has been exercised: Securitize Corp. declares no dividend, so the distribution path is untested on its own stock; the mint's ScaledUiAmount multiplier is 1, so no split has occurred; and no tokenized-holder proxy process or on-chain voting is documented. Two mechanisms are disclosed that are unusual and material. (1) FORK POLICY: 'In the event of such a fork, Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights such as voting, redemptions, and distributions. Tokens existing on other forked chains would not be recognized as valid representations of the securities' — a rare, explicit, pre-agreed chain-exception policy, and simultaneously a statement that the issuer, not the chain, decides. It adds that it 'would generally expect to follow the fork recognized by principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows' and that 'In extreme circumstances, Securitize may determine that migrating assets to an alternative fork is necessary'. (2) MANUAL FALLBACK: 'Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent' — an explicit off-chain recovery path that exists precisely because the chain is not the record. Emergency halt: PausableConfig on the mint, with no published policy for its use.

Two transfer agents, and only the tokenized one is an affiliate. (1) Continental Stock Transfer & Trust Company — SEC transfer agent File No. 084-00034, CIK 0000024179, DRS & DWAC #7808 — is the transfer agent of record for the Securitize common stock, named in the S-1/424B3 Description of Securities and in Securitize's own tokenize instructions, and independent of the issuer. No transfer-agency agreement for SECZ is published on either side, so the division of the books between them, and how the two are reconciled, rests on the issuer's own description.

links.label: Regulatory permission and disclosure

fields.value: The most heavily regulated of the three Solana-native issuers examined, and the only one where the tokenization vendor is itself the registrant. The underlying security is registered common stock of a Delaware SEC-reporting company listed on the NYSE (S-4 registration statement effective 2026-06-05; S-1 filed 2026-07-31, EFFECT 2026-08-07; 424B3 prospectuses 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-13). Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC is an SEC-registered transfer agent (File No. 084-06638). The S-1 describes the group as 'the only vertically integrated tokenization provider with SEC-registered entities across a transfer agent, broker-dealer, alternative trading system (ATS), investor advisor and fund administration'. Access to the tokenized form is intermediated by a regulated broker-dealer: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer' (note: the S-1 renders the entity name as 'Securities Markets, LLC'. RESOLVED 2026-09-17 against a primary source: Securitize's own 2026-07-02 press release names 'Securitize Markets, LLC, an SEC-registered broker-dealer and member FINRA/SIPC that operates an SEC-regulated Alternative Trading System (ATS)', so the S-1 wording is a typographical error in a registration statement and the gatekeeping broker-dealer is Securitize Markets, LLC). No exemptive relief or no-action letter for the tokenized form was located; the S-1 warns that 'market intermediaries may face unclear or evolving obligations'.

Delaware General Corporation Law governs the common stock and the share register; US federal securities law governs the listing, the transfer agent (Exchange Act §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21) and the broker-dealer/ATS gating access. No separate token terms of service or holder agreement for Tokenized SECZ was located; the operative public instrument is the Form S-1 prospectus risk factor plus the Securitize platform's general investor terms (not located in tokenized-SECZ-specific form).

Documents per-token whitelisting (tokenId required), wallet statuses 'ready, pending, failed' and 'not-authorised', and that 'whitelisting at token level does NOT require the wallet being registered at Securitize iD' (i.e. self-custodied addresses can be whitelisted).

C. subchapter V — the statutory basis for a tokenized register: §151(f) makes the rights of holders of uncertificated and certificated stock identical, and §224 permits the stock ledger to be kept on "1 or more electronic networks or databases (including 1 or more distributed electronic networks or databases)" provided it can produce the §219/§220 stockholder list

Continental Stock Transfer shareholder FAQs — the independent registrar's own procedures for the cases no Securitize document addresses: lost certificates (stop, surety bond, affidavit of loss and indemnity) and estate transfers (certified death certificate, notarised affidavit of domicile, medallion-guaranteed stock power)

Securitize Investor Help Center, "What if I lost access to my wallet?" - the issuer-side lost-key procedure for investors: email investorsupport@securitize.io, identity verification and a notarized affidavit; "We can recover most tokens from lost wallets" but recovery "may not be possible" in some circumstances. Generic to Securitize tokens, not SECZ-specific. Live page Cloudflare-blocked; text read from the Wayback capture of 2025-04-23 (identical in every capture since 2023-06-08).

conclusions.label: How value can leave the wrapper
conclusions.conclusion: Bidirectional switching between forms is asserted in one subordinate clause: "holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ". Only the INBOUND leg is documented, and it is a coordination between two transfer agents rather than an internal book movement: the holder asks their broker to move the shares out of street name "through the Direct Registration System (DRS) or Deposit and Withdrawal at Custodian (DWAC) method" to Continental Stock Transfer (DRS & DWAC #7808); Continental then "records you as the registered owner of the shares" and issues a statement; and only "Once your shares are registered directly on the transfer agent's shareholder ledger" can they be converted into tokenized form and issued to a Securitize-registered wallet. Securitize warns that "Not all brokers support DRS transfers" and that broker fees vary. The OUTBOUND leg — de-tokenization back to the Continental book-entry position — has no published procedure, burn address, processing time or fee anywhere, and the unquantified switch latency is the constraint the S-1 itself blames for potential price discrepancies between the two forms.

conclusions.conclusion: program-mediated, per-token whitelist. On-chain: Token-2022 DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified 2026-09-16), so every new SECZ token account is frozen at birth and only the freeze authority (8Twerer..., an apparent program PDA) can thaw it; plus PausableConfig for a global halt. conclusions.label: How shareholder economics pass through
conclusions.conclusion: Securitize markets corporate-action servicing as a core transfer-agent capability — the S-1 describes 'a comprehensive suite of securities services including real-time approval, record-keeping, distributions, dividend issuances and compliance solutions' — so the institutional machinery genuinely exists and is exercised for third-party issuers (BUIDL and others). For SECZ specifically nothing has been exercised: Securitize Corp. declares no dividend, so the distribution path is untested on its own stock; the mint's ScaledUiAmount multiplier is 1, so no split has occurred; and no tokenized-holder proxy process or on-chain voting is documented. Two mechanisms are disclosed that are unusual and material. (1) FORK POLICY: 'In the event of such a fork, Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights such as voting, redemptions, and distributions. Tokens existing on other forked chains would not be recognized as valid representations of the securities' — a rare, explicit, pre-agreed chain-exception policy, and simultaneously a statement that the issuer, not the chain, decides. It adds that it 'would generally expect to follow the fork recognized by principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows' and that 'In extreme circumstances, Securitize may determine that migrating assets to an alternative fork is necessary'. (2) MANUAL FALLBACK: 'Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent' — an explicit off-chain recovery path that exists precisely because the chain is not the record. Emergency halt: PausableConfig on the mint, with no published policy for its use.

transfer.mechanism: program-mediated, per-token whitelist. On-chain: Token-2022 DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified 2026-09-16), so every new SECZ token account is frozen at birth and only the freeze authority (8Twerer..., an apparent program PDA) can thaw it; plus PausableConfig for a global halt. Off-chain: the Securitize Connect API documents wallet whitelisting scoped to a specific token ('adds a wallet address to the whitelist of an specific token', requiring a tokenId, since 'in a given domain there may be multiple tokens'), with wallet statuses 'ready, pending, failed' and a 'not-authorised' response state. Notably the whitelist is NOT tied to a platform-hosted wallet: 'This is not required, as the whitelisting at token level does NOT require the wallet being registered at Securitize iD' — a self-custodied address can be whitelisted directly. Contractually: 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions', and specific Avalanche holdings carry business-combination lock-ups. US persons are the TARGET market here ('eligible U.S. investors'), which inverts the usual tokenized-equity geofence.

insolvency.headline: The holder claim is the registered share itself; transfer-agent and register continuity remain operational dependencies.
insolvency.holderStanding: The holder owns the actual registered common share. The S-1 risk factor is unambiguous on two points at once: 'we enabled Tokenized SECZ, a natively tokenized version of our common stock. Tokenized SECZ is not a separate share class' and 'Tokenized SECZ provides an additional mechanism for investors to hold and transfer shares in the Company'. The issuer's own press release adds that this is an 'issuer-sponsored tokenization of the same common stock trading on the NYSE' and that 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions.' Holders may move between forms: 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ'. There is no SPV, receipt or nominee layer in the legal structure — but access runs through a broker-dealer's onboarding, so whether the holder is a registered holder of record in their own name or a customer of the broker-dealer is NOT established by any document located, and this is the central unresolved question for this issuer.

operationalDetails.enforcementStanding: The person recognised on the official share register has shareholder standing; the token and transfer-agent process determine whether the wallet holder is that person.

insolvency.caveat: A contractual label such as “segregated”, “trust” or “first priority” is not treated as a court-tested insolvency result unless the dossier records that authority.

corporateActions.actions: Securitize markets corporate-action servicing as a core transfer-agent capability — the S-1 describes 'a comprehensive suite of securities services including real-time approval, record-keeping, distributions, dividend issuances and compliance solutions' — so the institutional machinery genuinely exists and is exercised for third-party issuers (BUIDL and others). For SECZ specifically nothing has been exercised: Securitize Corp. declares no dividend, so the distribution path is untested on its own stock; the mint's ScaledUiAmount multiplier is 1, so no split has occurred; and no tokenized-holder proxy process or on-chain voting is documented. Two mechanisms are disclosed that are unusual and material. (1) FORK POLICY: 'In the event of such a fork, Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights such as voting, redemptions, and distributions. Tokens existing on other forked chains would not be recognized as valid representations of the securities' — a rare, explicit, pre-agreed chain-exception policy, and simultaneously a statement that the issuer, not the chain, decides. It adds that it 'would generally expect to follow the fork recognized by principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows' and that 'In extreme circumstances, Securitize may determine that migrating assets to an alternative fork is necessary'. (2) MANUAL FALLBACK: 'Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent' — an explicit off-chain recovery path that exists precisely because the chain is not the record. Emergency halt: PausableConfig on the mint, with no published policy for its use.
corporateActions.caveat: Registration supports shareholder rights, but the operational channel for a token-held position must still be documented.

redemption.eligibility: Holders who have completed the broker-dealer onboarding: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer.' The issuer's press release adds that the tokenized form is for 'eligible U.S. investors' subject to 'onboarding, KYC/AML verification, jurisdictional eligibility checks'. Certain Avalanche holdings are additionally subject to business-combination lock-up agreements.
redemption.rails: Bidirectional switching between forms is asserted in one subordinate clause: "holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ". Only the INBOUND leg is documented, and it is a coordination between two transfer agents rather than an internal book movement: the holder asks their broker to move the shares out of street name "through the Direct Registration System (DRS) or Deposit and Withdrawal at Custodian (DWAC) method" to Continental Stock Transfer (DRS & DWAC #7808); Continental then "records you as the registered owner of the shares" and issues a statement; and only "Once your shares are registered directly on the transfer agent's shareholder ledger" can they be converted into tokenized form and issued to a Securitize-registered wallet. Securitize warns that "Not all brokers support DRS transfers" and that broker fees vary. The OUTBOUND leg — de-tokenization back to the Continental book-entry position — has no published procedure, burn address, processing time or fee anywhere, and the unquantified switch latency is the constraint the S-1 itself blames for potential price discrepancies between the two forms.
redemption.evidenceLabel: A redemption process is documented, but no independently observed completed redemption is recorded.

openQuestions: MINT ATTRIBUTION IS INFERRED, NOT PUBLISHED. Securitize has published no Solana contract address anywhere located. 5VzwKkvynPJzcgwhBe7ESEyNgqMbo15yBu7Sehssd9ED is attributed on the strength of its TokenMetadata URI pointing at metadata.securitize.io, matching name/symbol, the Token-2022 compliance extension set, a 2026-06-29 creation date (three days before listing) and a registry verified flag. That is strong circumstantial evidence, not issuer confirmation. Given four SECZ-branded impersonation mints on Solana, the single highest-value next step is asking Securitize IR to publish canonical addresses. Treat the address as high-confidence-but-unconfirmed until then.

Where is the $295M? Press reports $295M of tokenized SECZ; the Solana mint holds 148,998 tokens (~$1.24M). The S-1 puts locked-up business-combination shares on Avalanche, so the balance is presumably there — but Securitize publishes no per-chain supply figures and nothing reconciles the headline to the chains. The Avalanche contract address should be identified and its supply read to close this.

ANSWERED (2026-09-18): a tokenized holder is a registered holder in their own name, not a customer position behind the group's broker-dealer. Securitize's own tokenize instructions route the holder through direct registration BEFORE any token exists — the broker DRS/DWACs the shares to Continental Stock Transfer, "the transfer agent records you as the registered owner of the shares", the holder gets "an account statement or confirmation showing your name, account number, and the number of shares you hold", and only then can the position "be converted into tokenized form". Broker-dealer onboarding still gates ATS access and the whitelist still gates the wallet, but the ownership itself is direct registration. Residual gap: nothing published says whether the tokenized units are shown on Continental's ledger, on Securitize's control book, or on both.

What is the correct name of the gatekeeping broker-dealer? The S-1 says 'Securities Markets, LLC'; Securitize's broker-dealer is publicly known as Securitize Markets, LLC. Most likely a typo in a registration statement, but it is the entity that controls who may hold the security, and it should be confirmed against the FINRA/SEC BD registration rather than assumed.

Which entity holds the on-chain authorities, and under what program? 8Twerer... (mint + freeze) is an apparent PDA whose owning program was not identified; D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA... (permanent delegate, pause, split, metadata) was not resolved at all. Whether these sit with Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC (the regulated registrar) or with an operating affiliate matters legally, and whether the program has a timelock or multisig gate matters for grading. Fireblocks MPC is disclosed for corporate treasury only.

What are the 117 token accounts? 148,998 tokens across 117 accounts, with Jupiter reporting 44 holders and a top-holders concentration of ~11.7%. How many are investor self-custody wallets versus platform/custodian/liquidity-pool accounts is unknown. getTokenLargestAccounts on the public RPC returned HTTP 429 on 2026-09-16 and should be retried against a paid endpoint.

Who are the 'on-chain liquidity provision partners' on Solana? The S-1 says Solana trading 'is now enabled via on-chain liquidity provision partners' without naming them. Since holding SECZ requires whitelisting, a liquidity pool must itself be whitelisted — so the pool addresses, and whether pool LPs must be onboarded, are open. Jupiter reported zero volume in the 24h to 2026-09-16.

Is SECZ actually live as DeFi collateral? ANSWERED (2026-09-23): yes, on Loopscale. The second-largest SECZ token account, 6Nk983pK7GPa2FyVkj8crq3YQgbXZXA9wPipoBRY4Fhw (13,391.402983 SECZ at finalized slot 449676926), is owned by HUyo5aYaNQvodYmy8TmjnpcxQCk3PVsbyTJUyjmAihFx, a Loan account of program 1oopBoJG58DgkUVKkEzKgyG9dvRmpgeEm1AVjoHkF78 (Loan discriminator; DefiLlama's Loopscale adapter names that program as Loopscale). This matches Securitize's 2026-08-20 announcement that "Tokenized SECZ is now live within @Loopscale 's onchain credit markets on @solana" (as reproduced by The Crypto Times) for "Eligible holders". STILL OPEN: which price oracle values SECZ collateral and what a liquidation does when the liquidator's account is not on Securitize's allowlist (every new token account starts frozen), and whether the Loan account's token account was approved individually by Securitize. The protocols in the DeFi usage scan (Kamino, Jupiter Lend, Nest, Project 0, Save) do not include Loopscale, which is why this position was not in the scan.

Has the fork policy ever been applied, and who bears the loss? The S-1's fork provisions are the most developed chain-exception policy in this universe, but they allocate authority without allocating loss: nothing states what happens to a holder whose tokens end up on the chain Securitize does not recognise, or who compensates them. Also note the dependency it creates — the tie-break heuristic is whichever fork 'principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows' recognise.

How do dividends, proxy voting and splits work for a tokenized holder? Securitize sells 'distributions, dividend issuances' as transfer-agent services and runs them for third-party issuers, but Securitize Corp. pays no dividend, the ScaledUiAmount multiplier is 1, and no tokenized-holder proxy process is documented. Untested on its own stock. Note the earnout structure (VWAP thresholds of $15/$20/$25 triggering Securitize Earnout Shares over five years from Closing) will cause share issuance that must propagate to the mint — a live, dated test of the control-book-to-chain path.
What is the token-to-nontokenized switch latency and fee? Unpublished, and it is the constraint the S-1 itself blames for potential price discrepancies.

Has the Solana token program been independently audited? Nothing public ties an audit to this deployment, despite Securitize's scale (BUIDL alone was >60% of its tokenized AUM at 2025-09-30) and its 21-chain integration.

What is the de-tokenization route? The S-1 asserts holders "may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ" and the issuer publishes the inbound leg in full (DRS or DWAC to Continental, then issuance to a whitelisted wallet), but no document anywhere describes the outbound leg — no burn address, no request form, no latency, no fee and no statement of who bears the price risk while the position is in transit between the two forms.

How are the two registers reconciled, and which one governs? Continental Stock Transfer keeps the register of record for the common stock; Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC keeps the control book and master securityholder file for the tokenized units and is "the exclusive digital transfer agent". No transfer-agency agreement for SECZ is published on either side, so the division of the books, the reconciliation cadence and the tie-break on a discrepancy are all undisclosed — exactly the gap Bullish closes explicitly with its register-of-members tie-break.

PARTLY ANSWERED (2026-09-23): the Securitize help-centre article "What if I lost access to my wallet?" (investorsupport.securitize.io/hc/en-us/articles/7331990591127) is still Cloudflare-challenged live (curl, WebFetch, headed Chrome; the Zendesk help-center API redirects to /hc/en-us/restricted), but the Wayback Machine holds five 200 captures from 2023-06-08 to 2025-04-23 with identical text: "We can recover most tokens from lost wallets, however, there are circumstances where recovery may not be possible. links.label: Ownership of the underlying

fields.value: derivative

On paper: a membership interest in a designated Series of SHIFT DAO LLC whose sole purpose is to "acquire, hold, and maintain in its treasury assets whose economic performance corresponds to" one named index or stock. The Series 17 agreement says "Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets" and Art. IV.1 says "Series Members are granted treasury ownership only", with no voting, management or fiduciary rights. In practice three things break that chain. (1) The issuer's own site-wide legal notice says the opposite: "The Series tokens provide their holders with economic exposure to the value of the Series Assets; holding the Tokens does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets." (2) The executed Series agreements do not identify the token they govern - membership is obtained by holding a token "created from and constricted by the parameters defined in the Smart Contract located at an address and a blockchain to be determined" - so no published document links the SPL mint that trades on Jupiter to the Series whose treasury holds the asset; the Series 17 (S&P 500) agreement compounds this by requiring "at least one (1) TSLA Short SHFT Token". (3) What the Series is documented to hold is not the referenced equity but a daily-reset leveraged ETF share (Series 17: SPXL, Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 3x, ISIN US25459W8626; Series 12: Direxion Daily TSLA X2, ISIN US25460G2865), so exposure to Tesla or the S&P 500 is delivered through a third party's derivative fund. Graded as derivative for that reason; if the Series agreements' "owners in the Series Assets" language controlled and were bound to these mints, the record would move to spv-claim-redeemable.

Two custodians are named, in the Risk Disclosure only: "Each Series relies on DekaBank, a European regulated financial institution, and ALPACADB LTD, a U.S.-regulated broker, as custodians of the Series Assets." The Collateral & Custody page adds that backing is held "with FINRA-registered, SEC-regulated brokerage partners" in "dedicated accounts, separate from operational balances and from other clients' assets" and "off-balance-sheet". Marketing and press name Alpaca Markets as the brokerage rail. The holding entity itself is not named ("a private entity that holds the backing assets"), nor is the market maker that operates the B2B mint/burn endpoints, and no account, statement, holdings report or balance for any Series has been published.

links.label: Issuance and redemption

fields.value: Contradicted between primary documents. Each Series Operating Agreement grants a member a redemption right: "If a Member wishes to transfer their token back to the Series in exchange for funds, this is an internal membership-interest repurchase ... This transaction is available only to Members processed by smart contract where the transaction is settled directly from the treasury to the Member's wallet, not using any third-party assets." The Technical Overview says the opposite: "End users do not interact with the mint endpoint directly. Mint and burn are B2B endpoints used by professional market makers to maintain inventory. Users acquire Series Tokens by swapping on Jupiter against market-maker liquidity." U.S. and U.K. persons are excluded from membership entirely.

Documented retail path: internal membership-interest repurchase settled from the Series treasury by smart contract. Documented operational path: market makers mint and burn against the underlying ETF through B2B endpoints, 24/5 in line with U.S. trading hours, while user-facing trading is 24/7 RFQ on Jupiter, Meteora, Kamino and Orca. No burn address, latency, SLA or minimum is published for either path, and no SHIFT program exists on-chain to implement the smart-contract repurchase.

Primary market: "The per-token purchase price shall equal the executed market price paid in a bona fide transaction to acquire one (1) share of [the named ETF], plus a transaction fee equal to 0.1% of such executed price." Ongoing: "The Master DAO is allowed to charge operational fees to the Series using a percentage-of-treasury formula" - the percentage is never stated in the master or any Series agreement. Secondary market: "User-facing trading costs are reflected in the RFQ spread quoted by market makers", tightest in U.S. hours and widest at weekends; the two docs pages give different weekend ceilings ("up to ~3%" in Solution Overview, "up to ~5%" in Risk Management). No transfer fee is charged on-chain: none of the eight mints carries a transferFeeConfig extension.

links.label: Dividends and cash entitlements

fields.value: none

Nothing is passed through and nothing is applied by Shift. "Membership interests represent a limited economic interest in the Assets of the Series 17 treasury and do not provide any expectation of profit, income, or dividends." Leverage resets are the ETF issuer's: "SHIFT does not perform rebalancing. The leverage is delivered by the underlying ETF (e.g., Direxion TSLL), which manages its own daily reset internally. SHIFT simply tokenizes the ETF position 1:1. Nothing happens at 4 PM ET inside the SHIFT protocol." Wind-down is issuer-decided: on a "Master Cancellation Event" the Master DAO alone determines, in its administrative capacity, whether each Series "(i) continue[s] as an independent DAO LLC" or "(ii) be dissolved and wound up", and "all applicable fees, costs, and third-party expenses associated with such continuation shall be borne by the applicable Series or its members". Membership can also end involuntarily - "the person's involuntary immediate automatic withdrawal of their status as a Member, if the person is deemed a Restricted Person" - and Art. VII.2 provides that voluntary or involuntary cessation "does not give rise to any right of a Member to a distribution of any property or economic resources". Separately, the scaledUiAmountConfig authority on every mint lets the issuer restate all displayed balances; SOX3S already sits at multiplier 0.1.

links.label: Regulatory permission and disclosure

fields.value: Unregistered and self-disclaiming, on top of a real company-law registration. The site-wide legal notice states the tokens "have not been registered under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933 ... or under the securities or financial-instrument laws of any other jurisdiction", that the issuer "is not registered or authorized as an investment company under the U.S. Investment Company Act of 1940 ... and is not authorized as an Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), an Undertaking for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS), or an investment firm under the laws of any EEA Member State", and that the tokens are "not offered, sold, or distributed in the United States or the United Kingdom, nor to any U.S. or U.K. persons or entities; in applicable jurisdictions they are offered only to 'qualified investors,' 'professional clients,' or their equivalent legal analogues". The Terms of Use add that the membership interests "do not constitute public securities under RMI law, but purchasers are responsible for assessing their legal status in their jurisdiction". No prospectus, offering document or exemption filing was located in any jurisdiction, and no licence for the Series tokens - but a licence CLAIM does exist, on a different product's page. The vaults-only Terms state: "Shift DAO LLC is a corporate entity in RMI with an international investment business license and registration number 10246-26.", with a Majuro registered address (PO Box 852, Long Island Rd) and physical address (852 Lagoon Rd). Three things qualify it. (1) SCOPE: that page governs Shift Vaults - stablecoin staking and secured lending to a Cayman SPC - not the leveraged Series tokens in this dossier, and no licence claim appears in any Series Operating Agreement, in the Terms of Use, in the Risk Disclosure or in the site-wide legal notice, all of which instead deny registered or authorised status. (2) VERIFICATION: the number could not be checked against any Marshall Islands register - no public searchable register of RMI international investment business licences was located - so it is recorded as unverified, not as false. (3) CONSISTENCY: an investment-business licence, if real, would sit oddly beside the same issuer's statement that the interests "do not constitute public securities under RMI law".

Laws of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, stated in both the Terms of Use (s.12) and each Series Operating Agreement (Art. XII.2). Recourse is narrow: after a 30-day notice period a dispute "shall be settled by arbitration administered by the International Centre for Dispute Resolution", seated in the RMI, sole arbitrator, English, final and without appeal, and "No action at law or in equity based upon any claim arising out of or related to this Agreement shall be instituted in any court of any jurisdiction". The Terms of Use separately submit website disputes to "the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of RMI". Members owe and are owed no fiduciary duty (Art. IV.3, DAO Act s.109), and under Art. VI.2 (DAO Act s.111) "no one shall have the right under the LLC Act to demand to separately inspect or copy records" of the Series. A THIRD regime exists on the same issuer's vaults-only Terms, and it differs from both of the above: arbitration is "finally settled under the Rules of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce by one or more arbitrators appointed in accordance with the said Rules", with the seat "agreed by the parties" rather than fixed in the RMI, the same RMI governing law "without regard to its conflict of law principles", and - unlike the Series agreements - an express class waiver: "You agree that any disputes will be resolved on an individual basis, and you waive any right to participate in a class action lawsuit or class-wide arbitration." So one legal entity operates three inconsistent dispute regimes: ICDR with an RMI seat and a total court bar for a Series member, ICC with a negotiable seat and a class waiver for a vaults depositor, and the exclusive jurisdiction of the RMI courts for a website user. The Series agreements contain no class or consolidation provision at all, so collective redress there is unaddressed rather than waived - though sole-arbitrator bilateral arbitration reaches the same result.

conclusions.label: Who owes or records the right
conclusions.conclusion: SHIFT DAO LLC, a for-profit series DAO limited liability company. conclusions.label: Position if an intermediary fails
conclusions.conclusion: On paper: a membership interest in a designated Series of SHIFT DAO LLC whose sole purpose is to "acquire, hold, and maintain in its treasury assets whose economic performance corresponds to" one named index or stock. The Series 17 agreement says "Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets" and Art. IV.1 says "Series Members are granted treasury ownership only", with no voting, management or fiduciary rights. In practice three things break that chain. (1) The issuer's own site-wide legal notice says the opposite: "The Series tokens provide their holders with economic exposure to the value of the Series Assets; holding the Tokens does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets." (2) The executed Series agreements do not identify the token they govern - membership is obtained by holding a token "created from and constricted by the parameters defined in the Smart Contract located at an address and a blockchain to be determined" - so no published document links the SPL mint that trades on Jupiter to the Series whose treasury holds the asset; the Series 17 (S&P 500) agreement compounds this by requiring "at least one (1) TSLA Short SHFT Token". (3) What the Series is documented to hold is not the referenced equity but a daily-reset leveraged ETF share (Series 17: SPXL, Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 3x, ISIN US25459W8626; Series 12: Direxion Daily TSLA X2, ISIN US25460G2865), so exposure to Tesla or the S&P 500 is delivered through a third party's derivative fund. Graded as derivative for that reason; if the Series agreements' "owners in the Series Assets" language controlled and were bound to these mints, the record would move to spv-claim-redeemable.
conclusions.governingLaw: Laws of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, stated in both the Terms of Use (s.12) and each Series Operating Agreement (Art. XII.2). Recourse is narrow: after a 30-day notice period a dispute "shall be settled by arbitration administered by the International Centre for Dispute Resolution", seated in the RMI, sole arbitrator, English, final and without appeal, and "No action at law or in equity based upon any claim arising out of or related to this Agreement shall be instituted in any court of any jurisdiction". The Terms of Use separately submit website disputes to "the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of RMI". Members owe and are owed no fiduciary duty (Art. IV.3, DAO Act s.109), and under Art. VI.2 (DAO Act s.111) "no one shall have the right under the LLC Act to demand to separately inspect or copy records" of the Series. A THIRD regime exists on the same issuer's vaults-only Terms, and it differs from both of the above: arbitration is "finally settled under the Rules of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce by one or more arbitrators appointed in accordance with the said Rules", with the seat "agreed by the parties" rather than fixed in the RMI, the same RMI governing law "without regard to its conflict of law principles", and - unlike the Series agreements - an express class waiver: "You agree that any disputes will be resolved on an individual basis, and you waive any right to participate in a class action lawsuit or class-wide arbitration." So one legal entity operates three inconsistent dispute regimes: ICDR with an RMI seat and a total court bar for a Series member, ICC with a negotiable seat and a class waiver for a vaults depositor, and the exclusive jurisdiction of the RMI courts for a website user. The Series agreements contain no class or consolidation provision at all, so collective redress there is unaddressed rather than waived - though sole-arbitrator bilateral arbitration reaches the same result.

conclusions.label: Who can override token custody
conclusions.conclusion: Direct or one-signer control: Mint; Freeze accounts; Permanent delegate; Rebase / balance multiplier. Ultimate controller not established: Pause transfers, Claw back / burn.
conclusions.governingLaw: Laws of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, stated in both the Terms of Use (s.12) and each Series Operating Agreement (Art. XII.2). Recourse is narrow: after a 30-day notice period a dispute "shall be settled by arbitration administered by the International Centre for Dispute Resolution", seated in the RMI, sole arbitrator, English, final and without appeal, and "No action at law or in equity based upon any claim arising out of or related to this Agreement shall be instituted in any court of any jurisdiction". The Terms of Use separately submit website disputes to "the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of RMI". Members owe and are owed no fiduciary duty (Art. IV.3, DAO Act s.109), and under Art. VI.2 (DAO Act s.111) "no one shall have the right under the LLC Act to demand to separately inspect or copy records" of the Series. A THIRD regime exists on the same issuer's vaults-only Terms, and it differs from both of the above: arbitration is "finally settled under the Rules of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce by one or more arbitrators appointed in accordance with the said Rules", with the seat "agreed by the parties" rather than fixed in the RMI, the same RMI governing law "without regard to its conflict of law principles", and - unlike the Series agreements - an express class waiver: "You agree that any disputes will be resolved on an individual basis, and you waive any right to participate in a class action lawsuit or class-wide arbitration." So one legal entity operates three inconsistent dispute regimes: ICDR with an RMI seat and a total court bar for a Series member, ICC with a negotiable seat and a class waiver for a vaults depositor, and the exclusive jurisdiction of the RMI courts for a website user. The Series agreements contain no class or consolidation provision at all, so collective redress there is unaddressed rather than waived - though sole-arbitrator bilateral arbitration reaches the same result.
